title.zh: 卷三 魏書三 明帝紀
title.en: Volume 3: Book of Wei 3 - Annals of Emperor Ming
title.raw: 卷三 魏書三 明帝紀 Volume 3: Book of Wei 3 - Annals of Emperor Ming

sentences.zh: 明皇帝諱叡，字元仲，文帝太子也。

translations.literal: The Emperor Ming's taboo personal name was Rui; his courtesy name was Yuanzhong; he was the heir son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming—personal name Rui, courtesy Yuanzhong—was the crown prince of Emperor Wen (Cao Pi).

sentences.zh: 生而太祖愛之，常令在左右。

translations.literal: From birth Emperor Taizu loved him and constantly kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: From infancy Cao Cao (posthumously Emperor Wu of Wei) doted on the boy and kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：帝生數歲而有岐嶷之姿，武皇帝異之，曰：「我基於爾三世矣。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu states: When the Emperor was only a few years old he showed precocious intelligence; Emperor Wu considered him extraordinary and said, "Upon you I ground three generations of my house."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Shu relates that even as a small child he showed unusual promise; Cao Cao marveled and told him, "You will be the foundation for three generations of my line."

sentences.zh: 」每朝宴會同，與侍中近臣並列帷幄。

translations.literal: At every court banquet he attended together with them, standing alongside Palace Attendants and intimate ministers within the curtained inner chamber.
translations.idiomatic: At banquets and assemblies he was brought in with the adults, standing beside Palace Attendants and senior ministers inside the curtain.

sentences.zh: 好學多識，特留意於法理。〉

translations.literal: He loved learning and was broadly knowledgeable, paying special attention to legal principle and precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He was studious and well read, with a particular eye for law and jurisprudence.

sentences.zh: 年十五，封武德侯，黃初二年爲齊公，三年爲平原王。

translations.literal: At age fifteen he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wude; in the second year of Huangchu he became Duke of Qi, and in the third year Prince of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he received the title Marquis of Wude; in Huangchu 2 he was made Duke of Qi, and in Huangchu 3 Prince of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 以其母誅，故未建爲嗣。

translations.literal: Because his mother had been executed, he was not at first established as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Because his birth mother had been put to death, he was not immediately named successor.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：文帝以郭后無子，詔使子養帝。

translations.literal: The Wei Lue states: Emperor Wen, because Empress Guo had no son, issued an edict that this son should raise the Emperor [as his mother].
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Lue records that Empress Guo had no children, so Emperor Wen ordered her to adopt the boy as her own.

sentences.zh: 帝以母不以道終，意甚不平。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because his mother had not come to a proper end, felt deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: He still burned with resentment over the unjust fate of his natural mother.

sentences.zh: 後不獲已，乃敬事郭后，旦夕因長御問起居，郭后亦自以無子，遂加慈愛。

translations.literal: Later, having no choice, he respectfully served Empress Guo; morning and evening he had the senior ladies-in-waiting inquire after her health; Empress Guo, knowing herself also to have no son, thereupon increased her kindness toward him.
translations.idiomatic: In time he had no choice but to honor Empress Guo; each day he sent senior attendants to ask after her, and she, childless herself, responded with growing affection.

sentences.zh: 文帝始以帝不恱，有意欲以他姬子京兆王爲嗣，故久不拜太子。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen at first, because the Emperor was not pleased [with the arrangement], had the intention of making the son of another concubine, the Prince of Jingzhao, heir; therefore for a long time he did not invest him as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi saw the boy's discontent and for a time considered naming another son—the Prince of Jingzhao—as heir, so Rui went long without the crown prince's title.

sentences.zh: 魏末傳曰：帝常從文帝獵，見子母鹿。

translations.literal: The Wei Mo Zhuan states: The Emperor often accompanied Emperor Wen on the hunt and saw a doe with her fawn.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Mo Zhuan tells how he once joined his father on a hunt and came upon a doe and fawn.

sentences.zh: 文帝射殺鹿母，使帝射鹿子，帝不從，曰：「陛下已殺其母，臣不忍復殺其子。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen shot and killed the mother deer and ordered the Emperor to shoot the fawn; the Emperor refused, saying, "Your Majesty has already killed its mother; your subject cannot bear to kill its offspring as well."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi killed the doe and ordered the boy to shoot the fawn; Rui refused: "You have already slain the mother—I cannot bring myself to kill the young."

sentences.zh: 」因涕泣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept.
translations.idiomatic: He burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 文帝即放弓箭，以此深奇之，而樹立之意定。〉

translations.literal: Emperor Wen thereupon set aside bow and arrow; because of this he considered him deeply extraordinary, and his intention to establish him [as heir] was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi lowered his bow and was struck by the boy's character; from then on his mind was set on making Rui his heir.

sentences.zh: 七年夏五月，帝病篤，乃立爲皇太子。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, summer, fifth month, Emperor Wen was gravely ill; thereupon [Rui] was established as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer in the seventh year of Huangchu, as Cao Pi lay dying, Rui was at last named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi he assumed the imperial throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi he ascended the throne and issued a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 尊皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: He honored the Empress Dowager as Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was elevated to grand empress dowager, and the empress became empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 諸臣封爵各有差。

translations.literal: The various ministers received noble ranks in differing degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were ennobled according to their merit.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：帝與朝士素不接，即位之後，羣下想聞風采。

translations.literal: The Shi Yu states: The Emperor had had no previous contact with court gentlemen; after he ascended the throne, the host of officials longed to see his demeanor and manner.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi Yu notes that Rui had kept to himself before his accession; once on the throne, the whole court was eager to see what kind of ruler he would be.

sentences.zh: 居數日，獨見侍中劉曄，語盡日。

translations.literal: After several days had passed, he alone received an audience with Palace Attendant Liu Ye, and they conversed the whole day through.
translations.idiomatic: A few days in, he held a private, day-long interview with only Liu Ye, the Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 衆人側聽，曄旣出，問「何如」？

translations.literal: The crowd listened from the side; when Ye had come out, they asked, "What was he like?"
translations.idiomatic: Others strained to overhear; when Liu Ye emerged, they pressed him: "Well? What is he like?"

sentences.zh: 曄曰：「秦始皇、漢孝武之儔，才具微不及耳。」〉

translations.literal: Ye said: "Of the same sort as the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Xiaowu of Han—his talents fall only slightly short of theirs."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ye replied: "In the mold of Qin Shi Huang and Emperor Wu of Han—perhaps a notch below in sheer ability."

sentences.zh: 癸未，追謚母甄夫人曰文昭皇后。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei he posthumously bestowed the title of Empress Wenzhao on his mother, Lady Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei he posthumously ennobled his mother Lady Zhen as Empress Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，立皇弟蕤爲陽平王。

translations.literal: On the day renchen he established his younger brother Rui as Prince of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen his younger brother was invested as Prince of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 八月，孫權攻江夏郡，太守文聘堅守。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Sun Quan attacked Jiangxia commandery; the Grand Warden Wen Pin held firm in defense.
translations.idiomatic: That August Sun Quan struck Jiangxia; Grand Warden Wen Pin refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲發兵救之，帝曰：「權習水戰，所以敢下船陸攻者，幾掩不備也。

translations.literal: The court debated whether to send troops to relieve it; the Emperor said, "Sun Quan is practiced in river warfare; the reason he dares to go ashore and attack by land is to take advantage of our being unprepared."
translations.idiomatic: The court wanted to dispatch a relief force, but the emperor objected: "Sun Quan lives on the water—he only braves a land attack to catch us off guard."

sentences.zh: 今已與聘相持，夫攻守勢倍，終不敢久也。

translations.literal: Now he is already locked in a stalemate with Pin; between attacker and defender the odds favor the defender twofold; in the end he will not dare remain long.
translations.idiomatic: He is already tied down by Wen Pin; besiegers wear down faster than defenders, and Sun Quan will not linger.

sentences.zh: 」先時遣治書侍御史荀禹慰勞邊方，禹到，於江夏發所經縣兵及所從步騎千人乘山舉火，權退走。

translations.literal: Earlier he had sent Palace Assistant Clerk Xun Yu to console the frontier; when Yu arrived, in Jiangxia he mobilized troops from the counties through which he had passed together with the infantry and cavalry who followed him, a thousand men in all, ascended a hill, and lit fires; Sun Quan withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The court had already sent Imperial Clerk Xun Yu to comfort the borderlands; when he reached Jiangxia he mustered county troops along his route, took a thousand of his escort up a ridge, and lit signal fires—whereupon Sun Quan broke off the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太和元年春正月，郊祀武皇帝以配天，宗祀文皇帝於明堂以配上帝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe, spring, first month, he sacrificed at the suburban altar to Emperor Wu as counterpart to Heaven and sacrificed at the Bright Hall to Emperor Wen as counterpart to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Taihe 1, he offered the suburban sacrifice to Emperor Wu (Cao Cao) as Heaven's counterpart and honored Emperor Wen in the Bright Hall as God's counterpart.

sentences.zh: 分江夏南部，置江夏南部都尉。

translations.literal: He divided off the southern part of Jiangxia and established a Southern Jiangxia commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The southern portion of Jiangxia was split off and placed under a new southern Jiangxia commandant.

sentences.zh: 西平麴英反，殺臨羌令、西都長，遣將軍郝昭、鹿磐討斬之。

translations.literal: Qu Ying of Xiping rebelled, killing the magistrate of Linqiang and the chief of Xidu; the emperor dispatched Generals Hao Zhao and Lu Pan to attack and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Ying rose in Xiping, murdered the magistrate of Linqiang and the chief of Xidu; Generals Hao Zhao and Lu Pan were sent to crush the revolt and executed him.

sentences.zh: 二月辛未，帝耕于藉田。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day xinwei, the Emperor plowed the ceremonial field.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the second month the emperor performed the spring plowing rite in the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，立文昭皇后寢廟於鄴。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi he established a shrine-chamber for Empress Wenzhao at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi a temple for Empress Wenzhao was dedicated at Ye.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，朝日于東郊。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai he greeted the sun at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he performed the rite to the sun at the eastern suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙亥，行五銖錢。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, on the day yihai, he circulated the five-zhu coin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on yihai, the five-zhu coin was put into circulation.

sentences.zh: 甲申，初營宗廟。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen he first began construction on the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen work began on the imperial ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，夕月于西郊。

translations.literal: In autumn, eighth month, he greeted the moon at the western suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn he sacrificed to the moon at the western suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙寅，治兵于東郊。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, on the day bingyin, he drilled troops at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the tenth winter month he reviewed the army at the eastern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 焉耆王遣子入侍。

translations.literal: The king of Yanqi sent his son to attend at court.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Yanqi sent a royal son to the Wei court as hostage-attendant.

sentences.zh: 十一月，立皇后毛氏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he established Lady Mao as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Lady Mao was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 賜天下男子爵人二級，鰥寡孤獨不能自存者賜穀。

translations.literal: He bestowed on the men of the realm two ranks of nobility each; on widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless who could not support themselves he bestowed grain.
translations.idiomatic: Every male subject received two steps in rank; grain was granted to widowers, widows, orphans, and others unable to fend for themselves.

sentences.zh: 十二月，封后父毛嘉爲列侯。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he enfeoffed the Empress's father, Mao Jia, as a full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the empress's father, Mao Jia, was made a full marquis.

sentences.zh: 新城太守孟達反，詔驃騎將軍司馬宣王討之。

translations.literal: The Grand Warden of Xincheng, Meng Da, rebelled; an edict ordered General-in-Chief Who Inspires Awe Sima Yi (the Duke of Xuan of Jin) to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Warden Meng Da rebelled at Xincheng, Sima Yi was ordered to lead the punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 〈《三輔決錄》曰：伯郎，涼州人，名不令休。

translations.literal: The Sanfu Juelu states: "Bo Lang was a man of Liangzhou; his name was Bu Lingxiu."
translations.idiomatic: The Sanfu Juelu introduces "Bo Lang," a Liangzhou native registered as Bu Lingxiu.

sentences.zh: 其注曰：伯郎姓孟，名他，扶風人。

translations.literal: Its commentary says: Bo Lang's surname was Meng, his personal name was Ta, and he was from Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss identifies him as Meng Ta of Fufeng—"Bo Lang" was his nickname.

sentences.zh: 靈帝時。

translations.literal: It was during the reign of Emperor Ling.
translations.idiomatic: This was under Emperor Ling of Han.

sentences.zh: 中常侍張讓專朝政，讓監奴典護家事。

translations.literal: The Regular Palace Attendant Zhang Rang monopolized court government; Rang's overseer slave managed his household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Zhang Rang dominated the court; a steward-slave ran his household.

sentences.zh: 他仕不遂，乃盡以家財賂監奴，與共結親，積年家業爲之破盡。

translations.literal: Ta's official career did not succeed; thereupon he used his entire family wealth to bribe the overseer slave, joined with him in a marriage alliance, and over the years his family property was thereby exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Ta could not get ahead in office, so he poured his fortune into bribing that steward, sealed the tie with a marriage—and ruined himself over several years.

sentences.zh: 衆奴皆慙，問他所欲，他曰：「欲得卿曹拜耳。

translations.literal: The slaves were all ashamed; they asked what he desired, and he said, "I wish to obtain your company's bows to me."
translations.idiomatic: The humiliated slaves asked what he wanted; Meng Ta said he only wanted them to bow to him.

sentences.zh: 」奴被恩久，皆許諾。

translations.literal: The slaves, having long received his kindness, all promised.
translations.idiomatic: Indebted to him by then, they agreed.

sentences.zh: 時賔客求見讓者，門下車常數百乘，或累日不得通。

translations.literal: At that time guests seeking an audience with Zhang Rang—carriages at his gate often numbered in the hundreds, and some went days without getting through.
translations.idiomatic: Clients mobbed Zhang Rang's gate—hundreds of carriages—yet many waited days without an audience.

sentences.zh: 他最後到，衆奴伺其至，皆迎車而拜，徑將他車獨入。

translations.literal: He arrived last; the slaves waited for his coming, all went out to greet his carriage and bowed, and directly led his carriage alone inside.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Ta arrived last; the stewards rushed out, bowed at his carriage, and ushered only him straight through the gate.

sentences.zh: 衆人悉驚，謂他與讓善，爭以珍物遺他。

translations.literal: All were astonished, thinking he was on good terms with Rang, and vied to present rare goods to him.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd assumed he was Zhang Rang's intimate and showered him with gifts.

sentences.zh: 他得之，盡以賂讓，讓大喜。

translations.literal: When he obtained them, he used everything to bribe Rang; Rang was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Ta passed every gift on to Zhang Rang, who was delighted.

sentences.zh: 他又以蒲桃酒一斛遺讓，即拜涼州刺史。

translations.literal: He further presented Rang with a hu of grape wine, and thereupon was appointed Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A hu of wine sealed the deal—he received appointment as governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 他生達，少入蜀。

translations.literal: Ta fathered Da; in youth [Da] entered Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Ta's son was Meng Da, who went to Shu while young.

sentences.zh: 其處蜀事迹在劉封傳。

translations.literal: His deeds while in Shu are in the biography of Liu Feng.
translations.idiomatic: His career in Shu is told in Liu Feng's biography.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：達以延康元年率部曲四千餘家歸魏。

translations.literal: The Wei Lue states: In the first year of Yan Kang, Da led more than four thousand households of retainers to submit to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Lue records that in Yan Kang 1 Meng Da brought over four thousand households of followers and surrendered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 文帝時初即王位，旣宿知有達，聞其來，甚恱，令貴臣有識察者往觀之，還曰「將帥之才也」，或曰「卿相之器也」，王益欽達。

translations.literal: At the time of Emperor Wen, when [the king of Wei] had first assumed the princely rank, he had long known of Da's existence; hearing of his coming, he was greatly pleased and ordered eminent ministers with judgment to go observe him; they returned saying "He has the talent of a general," others saying "He has the capacity of a minister"; the king esteemed Da all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi had just taken the title King of Wei, he already knew Meng Da's reputation; delighted at his defection, he sent senior advisers to look him over—they reported a born commander, others said ministerial timber—and the king's regard only grew.

sentences.zh: 逆與達書曰：「近日有命，未足達旨，何者？

translations.literal: [The king] responded ahead with a letter to Da, saying, "Recently there has been an edict, yet it does not suffice to convey my intent—why?
translations.idiomatic: He wrote back at once: "My recent order barely hinted at my meaning—why?

sentences.zh: 昔伊摯背商而歸周，百里去虞而入秦，樂毅感鴟夷以蟬蛻，王遵識逆順以去就，皆審興廢之符效，知成敗之必然，故丹青畫其形容，良史載其功勳。

translations.literal: Of old Yi Yin turned his back on Shang and went to Zhou; Baili Xi left Yu and entered Qin; Yue Yi heeded the leather sack and slipped away like a cicada; Wang Zun read victory and defeat and chose his side—all discerned how dynasties wax and wane and knew how fortunes finish; hence painters set their faces on silk and historians inscribed their deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Think of Yi Yin leaving Shang for Zhou, Baili Xi quitting Yu for Qin, Yue Yi slipping away as legend tells, Wang Zun reading the times—they saw how dynasties rise and fall, so artists painted them and historians enshrined them.

sentences.zh: 聞卿姿度純茂，器量優絕，當騁能明時，收名傳記。

translations.literal: I have heard that your bearing is pure and abundant, your capacity surpassing; you ought to display your ability in a luminous age and gather your name into the records.
translations.idiomatic: They say your gifts are ample and your stature uncommon—you belong in a brilliant reign and merit a place in the histories.

sentences.zh: 今者翻然濯鱗清流，甚相嘉樂，虛心西望，依依若舊，下筆屬辭，歡心從之。

translations.literal: Now you have suddenly washed your scales in clear currents—greatly do I rejoice; empty-hearted I gaze west; lovingly as of old; putting brush to paper and linking phrases, my joyful heart follows.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have crossed into clear water I rejoice; I wait toward the west as toward an old friend, and every line I write follows gladly.

sentences.zh: 昔虞卿入趙，再見取相，陳平就漢，一覲參乘，孤今於卿，情過於往，故致所御馬物以昭忠愛。

translations.literal: Of old Yu Qing entered Zhao and on a second audience became minister; Chen Ping went to Han and on one audience rode as attendant-in-chariot—I today toward you feel affection exceeding former instances; therefore I send the horses and gear from my own equipage to display loyalty and love.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qing won Zhao's premiership on his second audience; Chen Ping became Liu Bang's companion after one meeting—I cherish you more than those tales warrant, so I send horses from my own stable as a token.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「今者海內清定，萬里一統，三垂無風塵之警，中夏無狗吠之虞，以是弛罔闊禁，與世無疑，保官空虛，初無資任。

translations.literal: It further stated: Now within the seas there is clarity and stability; the realm is unified; the three frontiers have no alarm of dust-storms; the central plains need fear no barking dogs—therefore nets are slackened and prohibitions eased, and the world is trusted; protector offices stand vacant with no assignments yet.
translations.idiomatic: The letter went on: the empire is settled, frontiers quiet and the interior calm—restrictions are relaxed and posts await men of talent.

sentences.zh: 卿來相就，當明孤意，慎勿令家人繽紛道路，以親駭疏也。

translations.literal: When you come to join me, you ought to make clear my intent; take care not to let your household swarm the roads, lest closeness alarm those who watch from afar.
translations.idiomatic: When you come, heed my meaning—do not clog the roads with kin and wagons and frighten observers.

sentences.zh: 若卿欲來相見，且當先安部曲，有所保固，然後徐徐輕騎來東。

translations.literal: If you wish to come for an audience, you ought first to settle your troops and retainers, establish something to secure yourself, then slowly come east with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: If you want a meeting, settle your troops and rear echelon first, then come east at an easy pace with a light escort.

sentences.zh: 」達旣至譙，進見閑雅，才辯過人，衆莫不屬目。

translations.literal: When Da had arrived at Qiao, his audience comportment was leisurely and refined; his talent in debate surpassed others; none among the crowd failed to fix their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Da reached Qiao, his bearing at audience was poised and his eloquence striking—all eyes were on him.

sentences.zh: 又王近出，乘小輦，執達手，撫其背戲之曰：「卿得無爲劉備刺客邪？

translations.literal: Moreover the king recently went out; riding a small palanquin, he grasped Da's hand, stroked his back, and teased him, saying, "Could it be you are Liu Bei's assassin?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Cao Pi went out in a small carriage, took Meng Da's hand, clapped his back, and joked, "You aren't Liu Bei's assassin, are you?"

sentences.zh: 」遂與同載。

translations.literal: Thereupon he rode together with him in the same carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Then he pulled Meng Da into the carriage beside him.

sentences.zh: 又加拜散騎常侍，領新城太守，委以西南之任。

translations.literal: He further additionally appointed him Regular Palace Attendant Who Roams at Leisure and concurrent Grand Warden of Xincheng, entrusting him with responsibility for the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: He named him irregular palace attendant and concurrent grand warden of Xincheng, charging him with the southwest.

sentences.zh: 時衆臣或以爲待之太猥，又不宜委以方任。

translations.literal: At that time various ministers some thought he was treated too liberally, and also that it was not fitting to entrust him with regional responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Some ministers felt he was rewarded too lavishly and unsuited to frontier command.

sentences.zh: 王聞之曰：「吾保其無他，亦譬以蒿箭射蒿中耳。

translations.literal: The king, hearing this, said, "I guarantee he has nothing else in mind—it is like shooting mugwort with a mugwort arrow."
translations.idiomatic: The king replied, "I trust him—it is like shooting mugwort with a mugwort arrow," meaning little threat.

sentences.zh: 」達旣爲文帝所寵，又與桓階、夏侯尚親善，及文帝崩，時桓、尚皆卒，達自以羈旅久在疆場，心不自安。

translations.literal: Da had both been favored by Emperor Wen and been on intimate terms with Huan Jie and Xiahou Shang; when Emperor Wen died, at that time both Huan and Shang had already died; Da himself, considering that he had long been a sojourner on the battlefield, his heart was not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Da had enjoyed Cao Pi's favor and been close to Huan Jie and Xiahou Shang; when Cao Pi died both men were already gone, and Meng Da—long a wanderer on the frontier—grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮聞之，陰欲誘達，數書招之，達與相報荅。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang heard of it and secretly wished to entice Da; he repeatedly sent letters summoning him; Da exchanged replies with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang learned of his anxiety and secretly courted him with repeated letters; Meng Da answered back.

sentences.zh: 魏興太守申儀與達有隙，密表達與蜀潛通，帝未之信也。

translations.literal: The Grand Warden of Weixing, Shen Yi, had a rift with Da and secretly memorialized that Da was secretly in communication with Shu; the Emperor did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yi of Weixing, who despised Meng Da, secretly reported a Shu conspiracy—the emperor dismissed it.

sentences.zh: 司馬宣王遣參軍梁幾察之，又勸其入朝。

translations.literal: Sima Yi the Duke of Xuan dispatched Army Advisor Liang Ji to investigate him and also urged him to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi sent staff officer Liang Ji to watch him and pressed him to come to court.

sentences.zh: 達驚懼，遂反。

translations.literal: Da was alarmed and afraid; thereupon he rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Panicked, Meng Da rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 干寶《晉紀》曰：達初入新城，登白馬塞，歎曰：「劉封、申耽，據金城千里而失之乎！」〉

translations.literal: Gan Bao's Jin Ji states: When Da first entered Xincheng, he ascended Baima Pass and sighed, saying, "Liu Feng and Shen Dan—holding a thousand li of metal-walled territory yet losing it!"
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao records Meng Da sighing atop Baima Pass when he first took Xincheng: "Liu Feng and Shen Dan held a thousand li of strongholds—and lost them all."

sentences.zh: 二年春正月，宣王攻破新城，斬達，傳其首。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, the Duke of Xuan broke Xincheng, beheaded Da, and sent his head [on display].
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the second year of Taihe, Sima Yi took Xincheng, executed Meng Da, and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：宣王誘達將李輔及達甥鄧賢，賢等開門內軍。

translations.literal: The Wei Lue states: The Duke of Xuan enticed Da's general Li Fu and Da's nephew Deng Xian; Xian and the others opened the gates and admitted the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Lue says Sima Yi turned Meng Da's general Li Fu and nephew Deng Xian, who opened the gates to Wei troops.

sentences.zh: 達被圍旬有六日而敗，焚其首于洛陽四達之衢。〉

translations.literal: Da was surrounded sixteen days and then defeated; his head was burned at the four-road crossroads of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After sixteen days under siege Meng Da fell; his head was burned at the great crossroads in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 分新城之上庸、武陵、巫縣爲上庸郡，錫縣爲錫郡。

translations.literal: He divided Shangyong, Wuling, and Wu county from Xincheng to form Shangyong commandery, and Xi county to form Xi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyong, Wuling, and Wu were carved out of Xincheng as a new Shangyong commandery; Xi county became Xi commandery.

sentences.zh: 蜀大將諸葛亮寇邊，天水、南安、安定三郡吏民叛應亮。

translations.literal: Shu's great general Zhuge Liang raided the borders; the officials and people of the three commanderies Tianshui, Nan'an, and Anding rebelled and responded to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang struck the frontier; Tianshui, Nan'an, and Anding rose for him.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：是時朝臣未知計所出，帝曰：「亮阻山爲固，今者自來，旣合兵書致人之術；

translations.literal: The Wei Shu states: At this time court ministers did not know what plan to pursue; the Emperor said, "Liang relies on mountains as fortifications; now he has come himself—it already accords with the Art of War's technique of luring the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion wavered until the emperor said Zhuge Liang had abandoned his mountains—the classical stratagem of baiting the foe now applied.

sentences.zh: 且亮貪三郡，知進而不知退，今因此時，破亮必也。

translations.literal: Moreover Liang craves the three commanderies; he knows advance and does not know retreat; if we use this moment, our crushing Liang is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Greed for those three commanderies will blind him to retreat—strike now and he is ours.

sentences.zh: 」乃部勒兵馬步騎五萬拒亮。〉

translations.literal: "Thereupon he arrayed horse and foot, fifty thousand, to oppose Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered fifty thousand horse and foot to meet Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 遣大將軍曹真都督關右，並進兵。

translations.literal: He dispatched General-in-Chief Cao Zhen to superintend the area west of the pass and jointly advance the army.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen was placed in command west of the pass and ordered forward.

sentences.zh: 右將軍張郃擊亮於街亭，大破之。

translations.literal: General of the Right Zhang He struck Liang at Jieting and greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He of the right wing crushed Zhuge Liang at Jieting.

sentences.zh: 亮敗走，三郡平。

translations.literal: Liang was defeated and fled; the three commanderies were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang retreated and the three commanderies were recovered.

sentences.zh: 丁未，行幸長安。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei he traveled in favor to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the imperial progress reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》載帝露布天下并班告益州曰：「劉備背恩，自竄巴蜀。

translations.literal: The Wei Lue records the Emperor's bulletin to all under heaven and proclamation distributed to Yizhou, stating: "Liu Bei betrayed grace and fled of himself into Ba and Shu."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Lue preserves an imperial bulletin denouncing Liu Bei for ingratitude and flight to Ba-Shu.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮棄父母之國，阿殘賊之黨，神人被毒，惡積身滅。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang abandoned the land of his fathers and mothers; he cleaved to the faction of cruel brigands; spirits and men were poisoned; evil accumulated and his person was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: It brands Zhuge Liang as a traitor who fled to villains—poison to gods and men, doomed by his own crimes.

sentences.zh: 亮外慕立孤之名，而內貪專擅之實。

translations.literal: Liang outwardly admires the reputation of establishing the orphan; inwardly he covets the reality of monopoly and usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he plays regent; inwardly he hoards power.

sentences.zh: 劉升之兄弟守空城而已。

translations.literal: The brothers of Liu Shan (styled Sheng) merely guard empty cities.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan and his kin are holding hollow shells of towns.

sentences.zh: 亮又侮易益土，虐用其民，是以利狼、宕渠、高定、青羌莫不瓦解，爲亮仇敵。

translations.literal: Liang further insults and treats lightly the land of Yi; cruelly he uses its people; therefore Li Lang, Dangqu, Gao Ding, and the Qingqiang—none failed to come apart like tiles, becoming Liang's enemies.
translations.idiomatic: His arrogance toward Yizhou and cruelty to its people have turned Li Lang, Dangqu, Gao Ding, and the Qingqiang tribes against him.

sentences.zh: 而亮反裘負薪，裏盡毛殫，刖趾適屨，刻肌傷骨，反更稱說，自以爲能。

translations.literal: Yet Liang wears the fur inside out and bears firewood—the lining is exhausted and the fur is gone; he cuts off toes to fit the shoe, carving flesh and injuring bone—yet he turns and praises himself, deeming himself capable.
translations.idiomatic: Like wearing a coat inside out or trimming toes for shoes, he ruins Shu yet boasts of skill.

sentences.zh: 行兵於井底，游步於牛蹄。

translations.literal: He maneuvers troops at the bottom of a well; he wanders in ox hoofprints.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigns from the bottom of a well and marches in hoofprints—utter folly.

sentences.zh: 自朕即位，三邊無事，猶哀憐天下數遭兵革，且欲養四海之耆老，長後生之孤幼，先移風於禮樂，次講武於農隙，置亮畫外，未以爲虞。

translations.literal: Since We assumed the throne, the three frontiers have had no incidents; still We pity all under heaven that it has repeatedly suffered arms; moreover We wish to nurture the aged of the four seas and rear the orphans and young of later generations; first We would shift customs through ritual and music, next drill martial affairs in the gaps of farming—We set Liang outside Our planning and did not take him as a worry.
translations.idiomatic: Since Our accession the borders have been quiet; We pitied a realm long wasted by war and hoped to succor the old and the young, reform customs through rites and music, and train armies between harvests—We scarcely counted Zhuge Liang a concern.

sentences.zh: 而亮懷李熊愚勇之智，不思荊邯度德之戒，驅略吏民，盜利祁山。

translations.literal: Yet Liang cherishes the foolish boldness of Li Xiong and gives no thought to Jing Han's warning to measure rival virtue—driving and plundering officials and people and thieving gain at Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhuge Liang clings to the rash bravado of Li Xiong and spurns Jing Han's counsel to weigh the enemy's moral strength; he sweeps up officials and commoners and plunders Qishan for advantage.

sentences.zh: 王師方振，膽破氣奪，馬謖、高祥望旗奔敗。

translations.literal: As Our royal army raised its banners, their courage broke and their breath was snatched away; Ma Su and Gao Xiang fled in rout at the sight of Our standards.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial host struck; Ma Su and Gao Xiang broke and ran at the first sight of Wei banners.

sentences.zh: 虎臣逐北，蹈尸涉血，亮也小子，震驚朕師。

translations.literal: Tiger ministers pursued the fleeing foe, treading corpses and wading blood—that Liang is but a petty fellow; he was stricken with terror before Our hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's champions drove the rout across heaps of dead—Zhuge Liang, that provincial pedant, quailed before Our armies.

sentences.zh: 猛銳踊躍，咸思長驅。

translations.literal: The fierce and keen leapt forward as one, each eager to drive deep.
translations.idiomatic: Every crack regiment burned to pursue without pause.

sentences.zh: 朕惟率土莫非王臣，師之所處，荊棘生焉，不欲使十室之邑忠信貞良與夫淫昏之黨，同受塗炭。

translations.literal: We consider that within the realm none are not the king's subjects; yet where armies march, brambles spring up—We do not wish loyal and upright folk in hamlets of ten households to share utter ruin with debauched factions.
translations.idiomatic: All lands owe allegiance to the throne, but armies leave wasteland in their wake—We would not see honest villagers perish alongside wicked courtiers.

sentences.zh: 故先開示，以昭國誠，勉思變化，無滯亂邦。

translations.literal: Therefore We first make Our meaning plain to display the state's good faith; think hard on turning back and do not cling to a traitorous regime.
translations.idiomatic: So We publish this warning in good faith: reconsider your allegiance and do not stay chained to a doomed insurrection.

sentences.zh: 巴蜀將吏士民諸爲亮所劫迫，公卿已下皆聽束手。」〉

translations.literal: All Shu generals, officials, soldiers, and commoners whom Liang has coerced—from ministers on down—may surrender with bound hands.
translations.idiomatic: Every Shu officer, clerk, soldier, or civilian pressed into Liang's service may lay down arms—from the highest minister to the lowest—and be received.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丁酉，還洛陽宮。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, on day dingyou, he returned to the Luoyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou in the fourth summer month the court returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：是時譌言云帝已崩，從駕羣臣迎立雍丘王植。

translations.literal: The Wei Lue states: At this time a false rumor spread that the Emperor had died; the attendants who accompanied the progress wished to install Prince Zhi of Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Lue reports rumors of the emperor's death and a plot among the entourage to enthrone Cao Zhi, Prince of Yongqiu.

sentences.zh: 京師自卞太后羣公盡懼。

translations.literal: From Empress Dowager Bian in the capital down to the high dukes, all were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The capital—from Empress Dowager Bian to the senior ministers—was panic-stricken.

sentences.zh: 及帝還，皆私察顏色。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned, all secretly studied his complexion.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor came back, everyone watched his face for a sign.

sentences.zh: 卞太后悲喜，欲推始言者，帝曰：「天下皆言，將何所推？」〉

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Bian was both joyful and grieved; she wished to trace whoever had begun the rumor, but the Emperor said, "All under heaven were saying it—whom could We trace?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Bian wept and laughed by turns and wanted the rumor traced; the emperor replied, "The whole realm was whispering it—where would I begin?"

sentences.zh: 赦繫囚非殊死以下。

translations.literal: He granted amnesty to prisoners held for crimes other than capital offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Noncapital convicts were offered amnesty.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，論討亮功，封爵增邑各有差。

translations.literal: On day yisi he assessed merit in the campaign against Liang; noble ranks and enlarged fiefs were awarded by grade.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi rewards for the campaign against Zhuge Liang were handed out—titles and added households according to merit.

sentences.zh: 五月，大旱。

translations.literal: In the fifth month there was great drought.
translations.idiomatic: May brought severe drought.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔曰：「尊儒貴學，王教之本也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month an edict stated: "To honor the learned and esteem scholarship is the root of royal instruction.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month an edict declared that reverence for scholars is the foundation of government.

sentences.zh: 自頃儒官或非其人，將何以宣明聖道？

translations.literal: Of late the instructors of the classics may not be the right men—how then shall the sagely Way be proclaimed?
translations.idiomatic: If the wrong men hold chairs in the academies, how can the sage's teaching be made clear?

sentences.zh: 其高選博士，才任侍中常侍者。

translations.literal: Select erudites of high quality whose abilities suit them for Palace Attendant posts.
translations.idiomatic: Choose outstanding erudites fit to serve as palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 申勑郡國，貢士以經學爲先。

translations.literal: Issue strict orders to commanderies and kingdoms: recommended candidates must give priority to classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Command every province to send up candidates grounded first in the classics.

sentences.zh: 」秋九月，曹休率諸軍至皖，與吳將陸議戰於石亭，敗績。

translations.literal: In autumn, ninth month, Cao Xiu led the armies to Wan and fought Wu general Lu Yi (Lu Xun) at Shiting; he suffered a crushing defeat.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, in the ninth month, Cao Xiu marched to Wan and met Lu Xun at Shiting—the Wei army was routed.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，立皇子穆爲繁陽王。

translations.literal: On day yiyou he established the imperial son Mu as Prince of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Prince Mu received the title Prince of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 庚子，大司馬曹休薨。

translations.literal: On day gengzi Grand Marshal Cao Xiu died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Grand Marshal Cao Xiu passed away.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，詔公卿近臣舉良將各一人。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, he ordered the high dukes and intimate ministers each to recommend one able general.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month each senior minister was to nominate one proven commander.

sentences.zh: 十一月，司徒王朗薨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Minister of Education Wang Lang died.
translations.idiomatic: In November Minister of Education Wang Lang died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，諸葛亮圍陳倉，曹真遣將軍費曜等拒之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Zhuge Liang besieged Chencang; Cao Zhen sent General Fei Yao and others to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: In December Zhuge Liang surrounded Chencang; Cao Zhen dispatched Fei Yao and others to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：先是使將軍郝昭築陳倉城；

translations.literal: The Wei Lue states: Earlier he had ordered General Hao Zhao to build up Chencang's walls;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Lue explains that Hao Zhao had already fortified Chencang.

sentences.zh: 會亮至，圍昭，不能拔。

translations.literal: when Liang arrived, he besieged Zhao but could not take him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang came he invested Hao Zhao but could not break the defense.

sentences.zh: 昭字伯道，太原人，爲人雄壯，少入軍爲部曲督，數有戰功，爲雜號將軍，遂鎮守河西十餘年，民夷畏服。

translations.literal: Zhao's courtesy name was Bodao; he was a man of Taiyuan. He was imposing in physique; in youth he entered the army as a company commander, repeatedly earned battle merit, became a general of miscellaneous title, and then guarded the west of the river more than ten years; Chinese and barbarians feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Zhao of Taiyuan (courtesy Bodao) was a formidable soldier who rose from unit commander to frontier general and kept the Hexi corridor quiet for over a decade.

sentences.zh: 亮圍陳倉，使昭鄉人靳詳於城外遙說之，昭於樓上應詳曰：「魏家科法，卿所練也；

translations.literal: When Liang besieged Chencang, he had Zhao's fellow townsman Jin Xiang outside the walls shout persuasion at a distance; Zhao answered Xiang from the tower, saying, "Wei statutes on rewards and punishments—those you have mastered;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang sent Jin Xiang, a townsman of Hao Zhao, to parley from below; from the battlements Hao Zhao shouted back that Jin knew Wei's laws well.

sentences.zh: 我之爲人，卿所知也。

translations.literal: as for what manner of man I am, you know it.
translations.idiomatic: "You know what kind of man I am."

sentences.zh: 我受國恩多而門戶重，卿無可言者，但有必死耳。

translations.literal: I have received much favor from the state and my house bears heavy obligation—you have nothing left to say to me; there is only certain death.
translations.idiomatic: He had received too much from Wei and owed too much to his clan—there was nothing to discuss but death before surrender.

sentences.zh: 卿還謝諸葛，便可攻也。

translations.literal: You may return and bid Zhuge Liang that he may attack at will.
translations.idiomatic: He told Jin to tell Zhuge Liang to attack whenever he pleased.

sentences.zh: 」詳以昭語告亮，亮又使詳重說昭，言人兵不敵，無爲空自破滅。

translations.literal: Xiang reported Zhao's words to Liang; Liang again had Xiang urge Zhao at length that men and arms could not match his own—there was no sense in destroying himself for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Jin relayed the reply; Zhuge Liang sent him back to argue that resistance was hopeless against such odds.

sentences.zh: 昭謂詳曰：「前言已定矣。

translations.literal: Zhao said to Xiang, "What I said before is fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Zhao answered, "My mind is made up."

sentences.zh: 我識卿耳，箭不識也。

translations.literal: I know you; my arrows do not."
translations.idiomatic: "I recognize you—my arrows will not."

sentences.zh: 」詳乃去。

translations.literal: Xiang thereupon departed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 亮自以有衆數萬，而昭兵纔千餘人，又度東救未能便到，乃進兵攻昭，起雲梯衝車以臨城。

translations.literal: Liang himself thought he had a host of several tens of thousands while Zhao's soldiers were barely over a thousand; he also calculated that relief from the east could not arrive quickly—thereupon he advanced to attack Zhao, raising cloud-ladders and battering rams against the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang, counting tens of thousands against Hao Zhao's thousand and assuming relief would be slow, pressed the assault with ladders and rams.

sentences.zh: 昭於是以火箭逆射其雲梯，梯然，梯上人皆燒死。

translations.literal: Zhao therefore used fire-arrows to shoot back at his cloud-ladders; the ladders caught fire and the men on them all burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Zhao answered with fire arrows; the ladders blazed and every man on them died.

sentences.zh: 昭又以繩連石磨壓其衝車，衝車折。

translations.literal: Zhao further linked ropes to stone millstones to crush his battering rams; the rams broke.
translations.idiomatic: He counterweighted stone rollers with ropes and smashed the rams.

sentences.zh: 亮乃更爲井闌百尺以付城中，以土丸填壍，欲直攀城，昭又於內築重牆。

translations.literal: Liang then built hundred-foot siege towers to overlook the city, filled the moat with earthen pellets, and wished to climb straight up the walls; Zhao further built a second inner wall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang raised hundred-foot towers, packed the ditch with earth to close with the walls, and Hao Zhao threw up an inner barrier behind the first.

sentences.zh: 亮足爲城突，欲踊出於城裏，昭又於城內穿地橫截之。

translations.literal: Liang bored tunnels as city saps, intending to burst up inside the walls; Zhao again dug a trench under the city and cut them off crosswise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang mined toward the town; Hao Zhao dug a counter-trench and blocked him.

sentences.zh: 晝夜相攻拒二十餘日，亮無計，救至，引退。

translations.literal: They attacked and resisted day and night for more than twenty days; Liang had no expedient; relief arrived and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty days of storm failed; when Wei reinforcements neared, Zhuge Liang lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉昭善守，賜爵列侯。

translations.literal: An edict praised Zhao's skill in defense and bestowed the noble rank of full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised Hao Zhao's defense and enfeoffed him as a full marquis.

sentences.zh: 及還，帝引見慰勞之，顧謂中書令孫資曰：「卿鄉里乃有爾曹快人，爲將灼如此，朕復何憂乎？

translations.literal: When [Zhao] returned, the Emperor received him in audience to console and praise him; turning to Central Document Director Sun Zi he said, "Your home region yet has such forthright men—if generals burn this bright, what more have We to fear?
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor turned to Sun Zi and marveled that Taiyuan could produce so fearless a commander.

sentences.zh: 」仍欲大用之。

translations.literal: He still wished to employ him in great capacity.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to promote him further.

sentences.zh: 會病亡，遺令戒其子凱曰：「吾爲將，知將不可爲也。

translations.literal: Soon afterward [Zhao] died of illness; his dying instructions warned his son Kai: "In serving as a general I learned how impossible it is to be a general.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Zhao soon died; he warned his son Kai how cruel the trade of generalship could be.

sentences.zh: 吾數發冢，取其木以爲攻戰具，又知厚葬無益於死者也。

translations.literal: I repeatedly opened tombs and took their timber for siege equipment—I also know that lavish burial does no good for the dead.
translations.idiomatic: He had plundered graves for siege timber and knew rich tombs brought the dead nothing.

sentences.zh: 汝必斂以時服。

translations.literal: You must wrap my corpse only in everyday garments.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a plain shroud—no finery.

sentences.zh: 且人生有處所耳，死復何在邪？

translations.literal: Moreover while alive men have their dwelling—what place has death?
translations.idiomatic: "The living have homes; the dead need none."

sentences.zh: 今去本墓遠，東西南北，在汝而已。」〉

translations.literal: Now we are far from the ancestral tomb—east, west, south, or north rests with you alone."
translations.idiomatic: "We lie far from the family graves—bury me wherever you must."

sentences.zh: 遼東太守公孫恭兄子淵劫奪恭位，遂以淵領遼東太守。

translations.literal: The Grand Warden of Liaodong Gongsun Gong's nephew Yuan seized Gong's position by force; thereupon Yuan was appointed concurrent Grand Warden of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yuan ousted his uncle Gongsun Gong as Liaodong governor and was confirmed in the post.

sentences.zh: 三年夏四月，元城王禮薨。

translations.literal: In the third year, summer, fourth month, Prince Li of Yuancheng died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth summer month of the third year of Taihe, Prince Li of Yuancheng died.

sentences.zh: 六月癸卯，繁陽王穆薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on day guimao, Prince Mu of Fanyang died.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the sixth month Prince Mu of Fanyang died.

sentences.zh: 戊申，追尊高祖大長秋曰高皇帝，夫人吳氏曰高皇后。

translations.literal: On day wushen he posthumously honored High Ancestor the Grand Coachman as Emperor Gao and Lady Wu as Empress Gao.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Cao Teng was posthumously titled Emperor Gao and Lady Wu as Empress Gao.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，詔曰：「禮，王后無嗣，擇建支子以繼太宗，則當纂正統而奉公義，何得復顧私親哉！

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, an edict stated: "By ritual, when the queen has no heir one selects a collateral son to continue the great shrine—then one ought to uphold the legitimate succession and serve public righteousness; how could one still look to private kinship?
translations.idiomatic: An autumn edict invoked ritual: a childless queen requires an heir from a collateral line—public duty must outweigh private affection.

sentences.zh: 漢宣繼昭帝後，加悼考以皇號；

translations.literal: After Emperor Xuan succeeded Emperor Zhao of Han, he added to Prince Dao the imperial title;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan followed Emperor Zhao on the throne he unjustly titled his father "emperor."

sentences.zh: 哀帝以外藩援立，而董宏等稱引亡秦，或誤時朝，旣尊恭皇，立廟京都，又寵藩妾，使比長信，敘昭穆於前殿，並四位於東宮，僭差無度，人神弗祐，而非罪師丹忠正之諫，用致丁、傅焚如之禍。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai was raised from an outer fief; Dong Hong and others cited the extinct Qin regime and confused the court of the day—they honored Prince Gong as emperor and founded his temple in the capital, while pampering a concubine from the fief like the Changxin Dowager, arranging generation order in the front hall and pairing four seats in the eastern palace—presumption beyond measure so that gods and men withheld blessing; instead they condemned minister Shi Dan's loyal remonstrance and brought upon Ding and Fu the holocaust of burning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai's advent unleashed Dong Hong's Qin-style sophistries—honoring a common father as emperor, twin temples in the capital, elevating a minor concubine beside the empress dowager—until Heaven turned away and worthy advisers like Shi Dan were silenced while the Ding and Fu clans burned.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，相踵行之。

translations.literal: From this time onward they followed one another in doing it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han repeated those mistakes one reign after another.

sentences.zh: 昔魯文逆祀，罪由夏父；

translations.literal: Of old Duke Wen of Lu inverted the sacrifice—the blame lay with Xiafu Ji;
translations.idiomatic: The fault for Duke Wen's illicit sacrifices fell on Xiafu Ji.

sentences.zh: 宋國非度，譏在華元。

translations.literal: Song departed from proper measure—the critique belonged to Hua Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Song's breach of ritual drew criticism upon Hua Yuan.

sentences.zh: 其令公卿有司，深以前世行事爲戒。

translations.literal: Let it be ordered that the high dukes and responsible offices take deep warning from former ages' deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers are to treat past errors as a solemn warning.

sentences.zh: 後嗣萬一有由諸侯入奉大統，則當明爲人後之義；

translations.literal: Should any successor someday enter from the rank of nobles to receive the great succession, he must make clear the duty of having become another's heir;
translations.idiomatic: If an emperor ever rises from a princely house he must honor his ritual adoption above blood ties.

sentences.zh: 敢爲佞邪導諛時君，妄建非正之號以干正統，謂考爲皇，稱妣爲后，則股肱大臣，誅之無赦。

translations.literal: whoever as flattering villain instructs a ruler of the hour and rashly establishes illegitimate titles against the legitimate succession—calling 'father' emperor and 'mother' empress—him shall the pillars of state execute without mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers who urge illicit imperial honors on birth parents will die at the ministers' hands.

sentences.zh: 其書之金策，藏之宗廟，著于今典。」

translations.literal: Inscribe it on metal slips and store them in the ancestral temple; record it in present statutes."
translations.idiomatic: The decree was cast on golden slips, lodged in the ancestral shrine, and written into law."

sentences.zh: 冬十月，改平望觀曰聽訟觀。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, he renamed the Pingwang Observation Tower the Observation Tower for Hearing Lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: The Pingwang watchtower became the "Listening to Litigation" tower.

sentences.zh: 帝常言「獄者，天下之性命也」，每斷大獄，常幸觀臨聽之。

translations.literal: The Emperor often said, "Prisons are the life-blood of the realm"; whenever he judged great criminal cases he habitually visited the tower to hear them in person.
translations.idiomatic: He called prisons the empire's lifeblood and regularly climbed the tower to hear capital appeals himself.

sentences.zh: 初，洛陽宗廟未成，神主在鄴廟。

translations.literal: At first the Luoyang ancestral temple was not yet finished; the spirit tablets remained at Ye's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Until Luoyang's temple stood empty, the ancestral tablets stayed at Ye.

sentences.zh: 十一月，廟始成，使太常韓曁持節迎高皇帝、太皇帝、武帝、文帝神主于鄴，十二月己丑至，奉安神主于廟。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the temple was first completed; he ordered Minister of Ceremonies Han Ji to take insignia and welcome the spirit tablets of Emperor Gao, Grand Emperor, Emperor Wu, and Emperor Wen from Ye; on day jichou in the twelfth month they arrived and were reverently installed in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: When construction finished in the eleventh month, Han Ji fetched the tablets from Ye; they reached Luoyang on twelfth-month jichou and were enshrined.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之按：黃初四年，有司奏立二廟，太皇帝大長秋與文帝之高祖共一廟，特立武帝廟，百世不毀。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi submits: In Huangchu 4 the relevant offices memorialized to establish two temples—the Grand Coachman Grand Emperor shared one shrine with Emperor Wen's distant ancestor, while Emperor Wu received a separate temple never to be destroyed through the generations.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes Huangchu 4: twin temples were planned—one sharing Cao Teng with a collateral ancestor, another immortal shrine for Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 今此無高祖神主，蓋以親盡毀也。

translations.literal: Here there is no spirit tablet for the High Ancestor—presumably because kinship ties were exhausted and it was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The absence of a "high ancestor" tablet reflects destruction after generational limits ran out.

sentences.zh: 此則魏初唯立親廟，祀四室而已。

translations.literal: Thus at Wei inception only kin temples were established—four chambers for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Early Wei therefore maintained four generations of close ancestors only.

sentences.zh: 至景初元年，始定七廟之制。

translations.literal: Only in Jingchu 1 were the regulations for seven temples fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The seven-temple system came only with Jingchu 1.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：事亡猶存，祭如神在，迎遷神主，正斯宜矣。〉

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: To serve the dead as if alive—rites teach sacrifice as though spirits were present; welcoming and transporting spirit tablets is precisely fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng approved: rites demand honoring tablets like living lieges—moving them to Luoyang was proper."

sentences.zh: 癸卯，大月氏王波調遣使奉獻，以調爲親魏大月氏王。

translations.literal: On day guimao King Bodiao of Great Yuezhi sent envoys with tribute; Bodiao was titled King of Great Yuezhi Friendly to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the Kushana lord Bodiao sent tribute and received the title "Yuezhi king allied to Wei."

sentences.zh: 四年春二月壬午，詔曰：「世之質文，隨教而變。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, spring, second month, on day renwu an edict stated: "The age's plainness or refinement follows teaching in changing.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu in the second spring month of the fourth year an edict declared that culture ebbs and flows with instruction.

sentences.zh: 兵亂以來，經學廢絕，後生進趣，不由典謨。

translations.literal: Since the turmoil of arms the classics have been cut off; youths advancing in ambition no longer follow the canonical models.
translations.idiomatic: War had extinguished classical studies—young men chased careers outside the canon.

sentences.zh: 豈訓導未洽，將進用者不以德顯乎？

translations.literal: Is it that instruction has not reached everywhere, or that those promoted do not shine through virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Had moral education failed—or did appointments ignore virtue?

sentences.zh: 其郎吏學通一經，才任牧民，博士課試，擢其高第者，亟用；

translations.literal: Those gentlemen clerks who have mastered one classic and whose talent suits governing the people—after the erudites examine them, promote those who rank highest with urgency;
translations.idiomatic: Court clerks who prove mastery of one classic and aptitude for magistracy—after examination promote the top scorers at once.

sentences.zh: 其浮華不務道本者，皆罷退之。

translations.literal: those who are flashy and do not attend to fundamental doctrine—all dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: Dismiss every candidate of empty cleverness who neglects the roots of learning.

sentences.zh: 」戊子，詔太傅三公：以文帝《典論》刻石，立于廟門之外。

translations.literal: On day wuzi he ordered the Grand Tutor and the three dukes to set up in stone Emperor Wen's Dian Lun outside the temple gate.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the Grand Tutor and three dukes were told to engrave Cao Pi's Dian Lun and set the stele before the temple gates.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以大將軍曹真爲大司馬，驃騎將軍司馬宣王爲大將軍，遼東太守公孫淵爲車騎將軍。

translations.literal: On day guisi he appointed Grand General Cao Zhen Grand Marshal, General-in-Chief Who Inspires Awe Sima Yi Grand General, and Grand Warden of Liaodong Gongsun Yuan General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Cao Zhen became grand marshal, Sima Yi grand general, and Gongsun Yuan general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，太傅鍾繇薨。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, Grand Tutor Zhong Yao died.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Zhong Yao died in the fourth summer month.

sentences.zh: 六月戊子，太皇太后崩。

translations.literal: On day wuzi in the sixth month the Grand Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi in the sixth month Lady Bian, the grand empress dowager, died.

sentences.zh: 丙申，省上庸郡。

translations.literal: On day bingshen Shangyong commandery was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Shangyong commandery was suppressed.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，武宣卞后祔葬于高陵。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, Empress Dowager Wuxuan Lady Bian was buried by affiliation at Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh autumn month Empress Dowager Wuxuan was laid beside Emperor Wu at Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 詔大司馬曹真、大將軍司馬宣王伐蜀。

translations.literal: He ordered Grand Marshal Cao Zhen and Grand General Sima Yi to campaign against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Cao Zhen and Sima Yi west against Shu.

sentences.zh: 八月辛巳，行東巡，遣使者以特牛祠中嶽。

translations.literal: On day xinsi in the eighth month he traveled east on inspection and sent envoys with a special ox to sacrifice at the central marchmount.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi he began an eastern tour and offered a black ox at Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：行過繁昌，使執金吾臧霸行太尉事，以特牛祠受禪壇。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu states: Passing Fanchang he had Bearer of the Golden Mallet Zang Ba act as Grand Commandant and sacrificed with a special ox at the abdication altar.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Shu adds that at Fanchang Zang Ba officiated as grand commandant and sacrificed at the Wei enthronement mound.

sentences.zh: 臣松之按：《漢紀》章帝元和三年，詔高邑縣祠即位壇，五成陌北，臘祠門戶。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi submits: The Han Ji records that in Zhangdi's Yuanhe 3 an edict ordered Gaoyi county to sacrifice at the accession altar north of Wucheng Lane at the year-end gate ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Pei cites Han Ji: Emperor Zhang once ordered sacrifice at an old accession terrace.

sentences.zh: 此雖前代已行故事，然爲壇以祀天，而壇非神也，今無事於上帝，而致祀於虛壇，求之義典，未詳所據。〉

translations.literal: Though this is a precedent earlier generations practiced, yet one raises an altar to sacrifice to Heaven—an altar is not a spirit; now there is no business with the Supreme Lord yet sacrifice is offered to an empty terrace—seeking in canonical meaning, the authority is not clear.
translations.idiomatic: Pei wonders why one worships an empty platform when Heaven is not confined to bricks—precedent does not clarify the rite."

sentences.zh: 乙未，幸許昌宮。

translations.literal: On day yiwei he visited Xuchang palace.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei the progress reached Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 九月，大雨，伊、洛、河、漢水溢，詔真等班師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month great rain fell; the Yi, Luo, Yellow, and Han rivers overflowed; an edict ordered Zhen and the others to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: September floods on the Yi, Luo, Yellow, and Han forced the Shu expedition to turn back.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙卯，行還洛陽宮。

translations.literal: On day yimao in winter, tenth month, the progress returned to Luoyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in the tenth winter month the court was back in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 庚申，令：「罪非殊死聽贖各有差。

translations.literal: On day gengshen an order stated: "For crimes other than capital offense, ransom may be paid according to grade.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen noncapital crimes could be redeemed for graded fines."

sentences.zh: 」十一月，太白犯歲星。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Venus encroached upon Jupiter.
translations.idiomatic: In November Venus passed Jupiter—an ominous conjunction.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛未，改葬文昭甄后于朝陽陵。

translations.literal: On day xinwei in the twelfth month Empress Wenzhen Lady Zhen was reburied at Chaoyang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On twelfth-month xinwei Lady Zhen was moved to Chaoyang tomb.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，詔公卿舉賢良。

translations.literal: On day bingyin he ordered the high dukes to recommend worthy and good men.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin ministers were told to nominate worthy candidates.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔曰：「古者諸侯朝聘，所以敦睦親親協和萬國也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict stated: "In antiquity the feudal lords paid court visits—that was how they thickened kinship ties and harmonized the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: An eighth-month edict praised ancient feudal visits that knit kin and realm together.

sentences.zh: 先帝著令，不欲使諸王在京都者，謂幼主在位，母后攝政，防微以漸，關諸盛衰也。

translations.literal: The late Emperor established regulations not wishing princes to remain in the capital because a young lord sits on the throne and the queen mother holds regency—one guards against gradual shifts and closes the sources of rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi had barred imperial brothers from the capital lest regencies invite faction—the policy guarded against gradual usurpation.

sentences.zh: 朕惟不見諸王十有二載，悠悠之懷，能不興思！

translations.literal: We reflect that We have not seen the princes in twelve years—how can the distant longing in Our breast fail to stir thought!
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years without seeing his brothers—the emperor confessed how sorely he missed them.

sentences.zh: 其令諸王及宗室公侯各將適子一人朝。

translations.literal: Let it be ordered that each prince and imperial-clan marquis shall bring one heir son to court.
translations.idiomatic: Each prince and dynastic marquis was to send one legitimate heir to the capital for audience.

sentences.zh: 後有少主、母后在宮者，自如先帝令，申明著于令。

translations.literal: If hereafter there is a young sovereign and a queen mother in the palace, they shall naturally follow the late Emperor's regulation, explicitly stated in the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a child emperor and a dowager ruled, the old rule would apply and be spelled out in law.

sentences.zh: 」十一月乙酉，月犯軒轅大星。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on day yiyou, the moon trespassed upon the great star of the Xuanyuan asterism.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the eleventh month the moon occluded the brightest star in the Xuanyuan constellation.

sentences.zh: 戊戌晦，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On the last day of the wuxu month there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Month-end on the wuxu cycle brought an eclipse of the sun.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲辰，月犯鎮星。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on day jiachen, the moon trespassed upon Saturn.
translations.idiomatic: On twelfth-month jiachen the moon passed Saturn.

sentences.zh: 戊午，太尉華歆薨。

translations.literal: On day wuwu Grand Commandant Hua Xin died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Grand Commandant Hua Xin died.

sentences.zh: 保塞鮮卑大人步度根與叛鮮卑大人軻比能私通，并州刺史畢軌表，輒出軍以外威比能，內鎮步度根。

translations.literal: Buzhugen, great chief of the garrison-keeping Xianbei, had secret dealings with Kebineng, great chief of the rebellious Xianbei; Governor of Bing Province Bi Gui memorialized and forthwith sent forth troops to overawe Kebineng without and pacify Buzhugen within.
translations.idiomatic: While peacekeeping Xianbei chief Buzhugen secretly dealt with rebel chief Kebineng, Bing governor Bi Gui sought to threaten Kebineng abroad and reassure Buzhugen at home.

sentences.zh: 帝省表曰：「步度根以爲比能所誘，有自疑心。

translations.literal: The Emperor reviewed the memorial and said, "Buzhugen believes himself enticed by Kebineng and harbors doubt toward himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read Bi's report and countered that Buzhugen felt manipulated by Kebineng and was insecure.

sentences.zh: 今軌出軍，適使二部驚合爲一，何所威鎮乎？

translations.literal: Now if Gui sends out troops, it will only frighten the two divisions into merging as one—how would that awe or pacify?"
translations.idiomatic: Dispatching troops would only scare both factions into uniting—hardly a policy of divide and rule."

sentences.zh: 」促勑軌，以出軍者慎勿越塞過句注也。

translations.literal: He urgently ordered Gui that whoever has gone out with troops must by no means cross the border past Gouzhu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He wired Bi Gui that no column was to advance beyond Gouzhu.

sentences.zh: 比詔書到，軌以進軍屯陰館，遣將軍蘇尚、董弼追鮮卑。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrived, Gui had already advanced the army and encamped at Yinguan; he dispatched Generals Su Shang and Dong Bi to pursue the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: The order arrived too late—Bi had already moved to Yinguan and sent Su Shang and Dong Bi in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 比能遣子將千餘騎迎步度根部落，與尚、弼相遇，戰於樓煩，二將敗沒。

translations.literal: Kebineng sent his son leading more than a thousand cavalry to welcome Buzhugen's tribes; they met Shang and Bi and fought at Loufan; both generals were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Kebineng's son escorted Buzhugen's people with a thousand horse and met the Wei generals at Loufan—both Wei commanders died.

sentences.zh: 步度根部落皆叛出塞，與比能合寇邊。

translations.literal: Buzhugen's whole tribe rebelled and went out beyond the garrison, joining with Kebineng to raid the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhugen's people bolted through the passes and joined Kebineng in border raids.

sentences.zh: 遣驍騎將軍秦朗將中軍討之，虜乃走漠北。

translations.literal: He dispatched General of Valiant Cavalry Qin Lang to lead the central army against them; the barbarians then fled to the northern desert.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Lang led the central host against them and drove the tribes into the northern sands.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，安定保塞匈奴大人胡薄居姿職等叛，司馬宣王遣將軍胡遵等追討，破降之。

translations.literal: In autumn, ninth month, Hubojuzihi and other great men of the garrison-keeping Xiongnu of Anding rebelled; Sima Yi the Duke of Xuan dispatched General Hu Zun and others to pursue and punish them; he defeated them and received their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Anding's peacekeeping Xiongnu chiefs rose; Sima Yi sent Hu Zun to crush and accept their surrender.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，步度根部落大人戴胡阿狼泥等詣并州降，朗引軍還。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, Daihu Alan chiefmen among Buzhugen's tribes went to Bingzhou to surrender; Lang led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month Xianbei leaders under Buzhugen submitted at Bingzhou and Qin Lang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：朗字元明，新興人。

translations.literal: The Wei Shi Chunqiu states: Lang's courtesy name was Yuanming; he was a man of Xinjin.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Shi Chunqiu identifies Qin Lang as Yuanming of Xinjin.

sentences.zh: 《獻帝傳》曰：朗父名宜祿，爲呂布使詣袁術，術妻以漢宗室女。

translations.literal: The Xiandi Zhuan states: Lang's father was named Yilu; serving as Lu Bu's envoy to Yuan Shu, Shu married him to a daughter of the Han imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiandi Zhuan adds that his father Qin Yilu served Lu Bu as envoy to Yuan Shu and married a Han princess.

sentences.zh: 其前妻杜氏留下邳。

translations.literal: His former wife Lady Du remained at Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: His first wife Lady Du stayed behind in Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 布之被圍，關羽屢請於太祖，求以杜氏爲妻，太祖疑其有色，及城陷，太祖見之，乃自納之。

translations.literal: When Bu was besieged, Guan Yu repeatedly requested of Emperor Taizu to take Lady Du as wife; Taizu suspected she was beautiful, and when the city fell Taizu saw her and took her for himself.
translations.idiomatic: During Lu Bu's siege Guan Yu begged Cao Cao for Lady Du; Cao Cao suspected her beauty and kept her when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 宜祿歸降，以爲銍長。

translations.literal: When Yilu returned and surrendered, he was appointed chief of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: After surrendering, Qin Yilu was made magistrate of Zhi.

sentences.zh: 及劉備走小沛，張飛隨之，過謂宜祿曰：「人取汝妻，而爲之長，何蚩蚩若是邪！

translations.literal: When Liu Bei fled to Xiaopei, Zhang Fei followed him; passing by he said to Yilu, "Another man took your wife while you hold office for him—how can you be so dull-witted!
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei withdrew to Xiaopei, Zhang Fei taunted Qin Yilu for serving the man who stole his wife.

sentences.zh: 隨我去乎？

translations.literal: Will you go with me?
translations.idiomatic: "Come away with us?"

sentences.zh: 」宜祿從之數里，悔欲還，飛殺之。

translations.literal: Yilu followed him several li, then repented and wished to return; Fei killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yilu followed a few miles, tried to turn back, and Zhang Fei cut him down.

sentences.zh: 朗隨母氏畜于公宮，太祖甚愛之，每坐席，謂賔客曰：「豈有人愛假子如孤者乎？

translations.literal: Lang was raised by his mother in the duke's palace; Taizu greatly loved him; whenever seated among guests he said to them, "Is there anyone who loves a foster son as I do?
translations.idiomatic: Qin Lang grew up in Cao Cao's harem; Cao Cao doted on him and boasted to guests of loving no foster son more.

sentences.zh: 」《魏略》曰：朗游遨諸侯間，歷武、文之世而無尤也。

translations.literal: The Wei Lue states: Lang wandered among the feudal lords and passed through the reigns of Wu and Wen without blame.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Lue says he drifted among the princes yet offended neither Cao Cao nor Cao Pi.

sentences.zh: 及明帝即位，授以內官，爲驍騎將軍、給事中，每車駕出入，朗常隨從。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming mounted the throne he appointed him to inner office as General of Valiant Cavalry and Palace Attendant; whenever the imperial carriage went out or in, Lang habitually followed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming brought him inside as valiant-cavalry general and attendant—always at the emperor's stirrup.

sentences.zh: 時明帝喜發舉，數有以輕微而致大辟者，朗終不能有所諫止，又未甞進一善人，帝亦以是親愛；

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ming delighted in impeachments; several times men suffered capital punishment for slight offenses; Lang to the end could not remonstrate or stop it, nor did he ever advance a worthyman for office—yet the Emperor for this reason was intimate with him;
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi loved harsh justice—minor faults earned death; Qin Lang never checked him nor recommended good men, yet the emperor loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 每顧問之，多呼其小字阿穌，數加賞賜，爲起大第於京城中。

translations.literal: whenever he consulted him he often called his childhood name Asu and repeatedly bestowed gifts, building him a great mansion in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He called him by his pet name Asu, showered gifts, and built him a palace mansion.

sentences.zh: 四方雖知朗無能爲益，猶以附近至尊，多賂遺之，富均公侯。

translations.literal: Though all quarters knew Lang could do nothing beneficial, still because he was near the supreme one many bribed him until his wealth matched dukes and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew he was useless, but proximity to the throne brought bribes equal to a noble's fortune.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：朗子秀，勁厲能直言，爲晉武帝博士。

translations.literal: The Shi Yu states: Lang's son Xiu was stern and outspoken; he became erudite to Emperor Wu of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qin Xiu, blunt and upright, later served as Jin Wudi's erudite.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》以朗與孔桂俱在佞倖篇。

translations.literal: The Wei Lue classifies Lang with Kong Gui both in the chapter on flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Lue pairs Qin Lang with Kong Gui among favorite sycophants.

sentences.zh: 桂字叔林，天水人也。

translations.literal: Gui's courtesy name was Shulin; he was a man of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Gui, courtesy Shulin, came from Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 建安初，數爲將軍楊秋使詣太祖，太祖表拜騎都尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jian'an era he several times went as General Yang Qiu's envoy to Emperor Taizu; Taizu memorialized and appointed him Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jian'an he ran errands for Yang Qiu to Cao Cao and won appointment as commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 桂性便辟，曉博弈、蹹鞠，故太祖愛之，每在左右，出入隨從。

translations.literal: Gui's nature was ingratiating; he understood board games and kickball—therefore Taizu loved him; he was constantly at his side, going out and following.
translations.idiomatic: Slick and skilled at weiqi and kickball, he became Cao Cao's constant companion.

sentences.zh: 桂察太祖意，喜樂之時，因言次曲有所陳，事多見從，數得賞賜，人多餽遺，桂由此侯服玉食。

translations.literal: Gui observed Taizu's mood; when he was pleased and enjoying himself, in the course of conversation he would subtly make suggestions—many matters were followed; he repeatedly received gifts; many people presented him gifts—Gui thereby wore marquis's robes and ate jade-like fare.
translations.idiomatic: He watched Cao Cao's moods and slipped in requests when he was merry—winning gifts until he lived like a lord.

sentences.zh: 太祖旣愛桂，五官將及諸侯亦皆親之。

translations.literal: Once Taizu loved Gui, the Heir's Household General and the feudal lords also all drew close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cao Cao favored him, Cao Pi and the other princes courted him too.

sentences.zh: 其後桂見太祖久不立太子，而有意於臨菑侯，因更親附臨菑侯而簡於五官將，將甚銜之。

translations.literal: Later Gui saw that Taizu long did not establish an heir but favored the Prince of Linzi; thereupon he drew closer to the Prince of Linzi and grew distant from the Heir's Household General—the General deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Cao Cao hesitate between heirs and favor Cao Zhi of Linzi, Kong Gui shifted to Cao Zhi and snubbed Cao Pi—who never forgave him.

sentences.zh: 及太祖薨，文帝即王位，未及致其罪。

translations.literal: When Taizu died and Emperor Wen assumed the princely rank, before he could visit punishment on his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi became king before he could settle scores with Kong Gui.

sentences.zh: 黃初元年，隨例轉拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangchu, following precedent he was transferred and appointed Commandant of the Coachmen.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu 1 brought routine promotion to commandant of the coachmen.

sentences.zh: 而桂私受西域貨賂，許爲人事。

translations.literal: But Gui privately accepted bribes from the Western Regions, promising to manage affairs for men.
translations.idiomatic: He took Western Regions bribes to fix appointments.

sentences.zh: 事發，有詔收問，遂殺之。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light an edict ordered him seized and questioned; thereupon he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Exposed, he was arrested and executed.

sentences.zh: 魚豢曰：爲上者不虛授，處下者不虛受，然後外無伐檀之歎，內無尸素之刺，雍熙之美著，太平之律顯矣。

translations.literal: Yu Huan says: Those above must not grant office emptily; those below must not receive salary emptily—then without are none who sigh like the woodcutter's song, within none who mock idle officials; the beauty of harmonious rule appears and the measure of great peace is manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huan warns that rulers must not sell offices nor ministers take empty pay—else integrity rots within and without.

sentences.zh: 而佞倖之徒，但姑息人主，至乃無德而榮，無功而祿，如是焉得不使中正日朘，傾邪滋多乎！

translations.literal: Yet flatterers only indulge the ruler until men without virtue gain glory and without merit gain stipend—how could this not make integrity dwindle day by day and crookedness multiply!
translations.idiomatic: Favorites who flatter the throne create honor without virtue and salaries without merit—no wonder honest men fade and knaves multiply.

sentences.zh: 以武皇帝之慎賞，明皇帝之持法，而猶有若此等人，而況下斯者乎？〉

translations.literal: With Emperor Wu of Wei's caution in rewards and Emperor Ming's adherence to law, still there were such persons—how much more those beneath them!"
translations.idiomatic: If even cautious Cao Cao and strict Mingdi bred such men, what of lesser courts?"

sentences.zh: 十二月，公孫淵斬送孫權所遣使張彌、許晏首，以淵爲大司馬樂浪公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Gongsun Yuan beheaded and forwarded the heads of Sun Quan's envoys Zhang Mi and Xu Yan; Yuan was appointed Grand Marshal and Duke of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: In December Gongsun Yuan sent Sun Quan's envoys Zhang Mi and Xu Yan's heads to Luoyang and received grand marshal and Duke of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：并州刺史畢軌送漢故度遼將軍范明友鮮卑奴，年三百五十歲，言語飲食如常人。

translations.literal: The Shi Yu states: Governor of Bing Province Bi Gui presented a former Han Colonel Who Crossed the Liao Fan Mingyou's Xianbei slave, aged three hundred fifty years, whose speech and eating were like an ordinary person's.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Gui reportedly offered a 350-year-old Xianbei slave of Fan Mingyou who ate and spoke like any man.

sentences.zh: 奴云：「霍顯，光後小妻。

translations.literal: The slave said: "Huo Xian was Guang's junior wife after his principal wife died.
translations.idiomatic: The slave claimed Huo Xian was Huo Guang's concubine.

sentences.zh: 明友妻，光前妻女。

translations.literal: Mingyou's wife was the daughter of Guang's former principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Mingyou's wife was a daughter of Huo Guang's first wife.

sentences.zh: 」《博物志》曰：時京邑有一人失其姓名，食啖兼十許人，遂肥不能動。

translations.literal: The Bowuzhi states: At that time in the capital there was a man who lost his name; he ate enough for more than ten men and grew so fat he could not move.
translations.idiomatic: The Bowuzhi tells of a glutton in the capital who ate for ten and grew immobile.

sentences.zh: 其父曾作遠方長吏，官徙送彼縣，令故義傳供食之；

translations.literal: His father had once served as a distant magistrate; when the office transferred they sent him to that county and ordered old associates to supply his food;
translations.idiomatic: His father, a transferred official, left him to be fed by county hosts.

sentences.zh: 一二年中，一鄉中輒爲之儉。

translations.literal: within a year or two the whole canton was drained by him.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years he beggared the whole district.

sentences.zh: 《傅子》曰：時太原發冢破棺，棺中有一生婦人，將出與語，生人也。

translations.literal: The Fu Zi states: At that time in Taiyuan they opened a tomb and broke the coffin; inside was a living woman; when they brought her out and spoke with her, she was alive.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu Zi records a living woman unearthed from a Taiyuan tomb.

sentences.zh: 送之京師，問其本事，不知也。

translations.literal: They sent her to the capital; asked her origins—she did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Luoyang, she remembered nothing of her past.

sentences.zh: 視其冢上樹木可三十歲，不知此婦人三十歲常生於地中邪？

translations.literal: They looked at the trees on her mound—about thirty years old—did this woman for thirty years constantly live in the earth?
translations.idiomatic: The mound's trees were only thirty years old—had she lain underground three decades?

sentences.zh: 將一朝欻生，偶與發冢者會也？〉

translations.literal: Or did she suddenly come to life one morning and happen to meet the tomb-openers?"
translations.idiomatic: Or had she revived overnight when grave robbers broke in?"

sentences.zh: 二年春二月乙未，太白犯熒惑。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, second month, on day yiwei Venus trespassed upon Mars.
