translations.idiomatic: On yiwei in the second spring month Venus passed Mars.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，詔曰：「鞭作官刑，所以糾慢怠也，而頃多以無辜死。

translations.literal: On day guiyou an edict stated: "The whip as official punishment exists to correct slackness and negligence; yet recently many innocents have died under it.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou an edict noted that judicial flogging had killed the innocent too often.

sentences.zh: 其減鞭杖之制，著于令。

translations.literal: Reduce the regulations for whip and staff—record it in the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Flogging rules were to be softened and codified.

sentences.zh: 」三月庚寅，山陽公薨，帝素服發哀，遣使持節典護喪事。

translations.literal: On day gengyin in the third month the Duke of Shanyang died; the Emperor wore plain sackcloth and sounded mourning; he dispatched envoys with insignia to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: On third-month gengyin Emperor Xian died; Mingdi mourned in white and sent officers to manage the rites.

sentences.zh: 己酉，大赦。

translations.literal: On day jiyou a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou came a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，大疫。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, a great pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Summer brought a terrible plague.

sentences.zh: 崇華殿災。

translations.literal: The Chonghua Hall burned.
translations.idiomatic: Fire destroyed Chonghua Hall.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，詔有司以太牢告祠文帝廟。

translations.literal: On day bingyin he ordered the relevant offices to announce with a bull sacrifice at Emperor Wen's temple.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin officials sacrificed an ox at Cao Pi's shrine.

sentences.zh: 追謚山陽公爲漢孝獻皇帝，葬以漢禮。

translations.literal: He posthumously titled the Duke of Shanyang as Emperor Xiaoxian of Han and buried him with Han ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The abdicated Han sovereign received posthumous title Emperor Xiaoxian and a Han-style burial.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝傳》曰：帝變服，率羣臣哭之，使使持節行司徒太常和洽弔祭，又使持節行大司空大司農崔林監護喪事。

translations.literal: The Xiandi Zhuan states: The Emperor changed garments, led the host of ministers in weeping, sent Minister of Education acting Minister of Ceremonies He Qia with insignia to condole and sacrifice, and sent Minister of Works acting Minister of Agriculture Cui Lin with insignia to supervise the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiandi Zhuan adds that Mingdi wore mourning, wept with his ministers, and sent He Qia and Cui Lin to officiate.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「蓋五帝之事尚矣，仲尼盛稱堯、舜巍巍蕩蕩之功者，以爲禪代乃大聖之懿事也。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The affairs of the Five Emperors lie remote; Confucius greatly praised Yao and Shun's lofty, vast deeds because abdication is the fine affair of great sages.
translations.idiomatic: An edict quoted Confucius on Yao and Shun to frame abdication as the noblest transfer of power.

sentences.zh: 山陽公深識天祿永終之運，禪位文皇帝以順天命。

translations.literal: The Duke of Shanyang deeply understood the movement of Heaven's mandate reaching its end and yielded the throne to Emperor Wen to obey Heaven's command.
translations.idiomatic: It praised Emperor Xian for seeing Han's mandate expire and yielding to Cao Pi.

sentences.zh: 先帝命公行漢正朔，郊天祀祖以天子之禮，言事不稱臣，此舜事堯之義也。

translations.literal: The late Emperor ordered the Duke to observe Han's calendar in his state, sacrifice to Heaven and ancestors with the Son of Heaven's rites, and present memorials without styling himself subject—this is the righteousness of Shun serving Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi had let him keep Han rites and calendar as Yao had indulged Shun.

sentences.zh: 昔放勛殂落，四海如喪考妣，遏密八音，明喪葬之禮同於王者也。

translations.literal: Of old when Fangxun passed away, within the four seas it was as if they had lost father and mother; they silenced the eight musical instruments—making clear that burial rites matched the king's.
translations.idiomatic: It cited Yao's death—universal grief and silenced music—to justify imperial funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 今有司奏喪禮比諸侯王，此豈古之遺制而先帝之至意哉？

translations.literal: Now the relevant offices memorialize that mourning ritual should compare to feudal kings—is this an ancient surviving regulation and the late Emperor's utmost intent?
translations.idiomatic: The court had proposed mere kingly rites—Mingdi asked whether that honored Cao Pi's promise.

sentences.zh: 今謚公漢孝獻皇帝。

translations.literal: Now We posthumously title the Duke Emperor Xiaoxian of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore elevated the duke to Emperor Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 」使太尉具以一太牢告祠文帝廟，曰：「叡聞夫禮也者，反本請吉，不忘厥初，是以先代之君，尊尊親親，戚有尚焉。

translations.literal: He ordered the Grand Commandant to report with one bull at Emperor Wen's temple, saying: "Rui has heard that ritual turns back to the root and seeks good fortune, not forgetting its beginning—therefore former ages' rulers honored forebears and kin according to degree.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant was to sacrifice at Cao Pi's shrine while Mingdi spoke of ritual roots and filial duty.

sentences.zh: 今山陽公寢疾棄國，有司建言喪紀之禮視諸侯王。

translations.literal: Now the Duke of Shanyang lies ill and has cast aside his state; the relevant offices propose mourning observances like those for feudal kings.
translations.idiomatic: Officials had ranked the funeral as for a mere king.

sentences.zh: 叡惟山陽公昔知天命永終於己，深觀歷數允在聖躬，傳祚禪位，尊我民主，斯乃陶唐懿德之事也。

translations.literal: Rui reflects that the Duke of Shanyang long ago knew Heaven's mandate had ended with himself; he deeply observed that the succession rested with the sage person; he transmitted the register and yielded the throne, honoring Our people's ruler—this is the fine deed of lofty Tang virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi insisted Emperor Xian had knowingly surrendered the mandate to Wei.

sentences.zh: 黃初受終，命公于國行漢正朔，郊天祀祖禮樂制度率乃漢舊，斯亦舜、禹明堂之義也。

translations.literal: In Huangchu receiving the end, he ordered the Duke in his state to follow Han's calendar; sacrifice to Heaven and ancestors, ritual and music and institutions all followed Han's old—this too is the righteousness of Shun and Yu in the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu had preserved Han ritual inside the duchy—like Shun and Yu's precedent.

sentences.zh: 上考遂初，皇極攸建，允熙克讓，莫明于茲。

translations.literal: Looking upward to examine the origin, the imperial pivot was founded; trusting in yielding and modesty, none was clearer than this.
translations.idiomatic: He praised the abdication as the clearest act of yielding.

sentences.zh: 蓋子以繼志嗣訓爲孝，臣以配命欽述爲忠，故詩稱『匪棘其猶，聿追來孝』，書曰『前人受命，茲不忘大功』。

translations.literal: The son takes continuing the intent and inheriting the teaching as filial piety; the minister takes matching the charge and reverently narrating as loyalty—therefore the Poetry says 'Be not anxious about far plans—pursue the filial duty coming behind'; the Document says 'The former men received the charge—forget not the great merit.'
translations.idiomatic: He cited the Classic of Poetry and Documents on filial succession and loyal commemoration.

sentences.zh: 叡敢不奉承徽典，以昭皇考之神靈。

translations.literal: How dare Rui not uphold the splendid precedents to manifest the spirit of the August Father?
translations.idiomatic: He vowed to fulfill his father's compact with the abdicated house.

sentences.zh: 今追謚山陽公曰孝獻皇帝，冊贈璽紱。

translations.literal: Now We posthumously title the Duke of Shanyang Emperor Xiaoxian and confer patent and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He granted posthumous title, patent, and ribbons.

sentences.zh: 命司徒、司空持節弔祭護喪，光祿、大鴻臚爲副，將作大匠、復土將軍營成陵墓，及置百官羣吏，車旗服章喪葬禮儀，一如漢氏故事；

translations.literal: He ordered the Minister of Education and Minister of Works to hold insignia and condole and sacrifice and supervise the funeral, with Minister of the Household and Grand Herald as deputies; the Corps Director and General Who Covers the Earth shall construct the mausoleum and tombs, and establish the hundred officials and clerks; carriage banners, dress insignia, and funeral ritual—all according to Han precedent;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers would officiate, engineers build the mausoleum, and Han-era funeral standards applied throughout.

sentences.zh: 喪葬所供羣官之費，皆仰大司農。

translations.literal: the expenses for funeral supplies for the host of officials shall all look to the Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of agriculture funded officials' funeral expenses.

sentences.zh: 立其後嗣爲山陽公，以通三統，永爲魏賔。

translations.literal: Establish his later heir as Duke of Shanyang to link the Three Systems and forever be Wei's guest.
translations.idiomatic: A new Duke of Shanyang would continue the Han line as Wei's ceremonial ally.

sentences.zh: 」於是贈冊曰：「嗚呼，昔皇天降戾于漢，俾逆臣董卓，播厥凶虐，焚滅京都，劫遷大駕。

translations.literal: Thereupon the patent read: "Alas—of old August Heaven sent calamity upon Han, enabling the rebellious minister Dong Zhuo to spread his fierce cruelty, burn and destroy the capital, and seize and move the great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The patent lamented Dong Zhuo's sack of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 于時六合雲擾，姦雄熛起。

translations.literal: At that time within the six directions clouds rose in turmoil and villain heroes blazed up.
translations.idiomatic: Chaos followed across the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝自西京，徂唯求定，臻茲洛邑。

translations.literal: The Emperor from the western capital went only seeking stability until he reached this Luoyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Han emperor fled west, then settled at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 疇咨聖賢，聿改乘轅，又遷許昌，武皇帝是依。

translations.literal: He consulted worthies and sages, then changed the royal carriage and again moved to Xuchang—leaning on Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He sought advisers, moved court to Xu, and relied on Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 歲在玄枵，皇師肇征，迄于鶉尾，十有八載，羣寇殲殄，九域咸乂。

translations.literal: In the year-star's station Xuanyuan the royal army first campaigned; until the year-star reached Quwei—eighteen years—the bandit hosts were exterminated and the nine regions all ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen years of campaigns crushed the warlords and pacified the nine provinces.

sentences.zh: 惟帝念功，祚茲魏國，大啟土宇。

translations.literal: The Emperor mindful of merit founded this Wei state and greatly opened soil and territory.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded merit by founding Wei.

sentences.zh: 爰及文皇帝，齊聖廣淵，仁聲旁流，柔遠能邇，殊俗向義，乾精承祚，坤靈吐曜，稽極玉衡，允膺歷數，度于軌儀，克猒帝心。

translations.literal: Continuing to Emperor Wen—equal sagehood, vast and deep—his humane fame flowed abroad; he softened the distant and could manage the near; alien customs turned to righteousness; celestial essence received the register and earthly spirits spat radiance; examining the pole and jade sight-tube, he truly bore the succession and measured by standards and pattern—he could satisfy the imperial heart.
translations.idiomatic: It hymned Cao Pi's virtue, cosmology, and right to the throne.

sentences.zh: 乃仰欽七政，俯察五典，弗采四嶽之謀，不俟師錫之舉，幽贊神明，承天禪位。

translations.literal: Then looking up he revered the seven luminaries; looking down he examined the five canons; he did not adopt the four marchlords' counsel nor await the masters' elevation—secretly assisted by spirits he received Heaven's abdicated throne.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi needed no Yao-Shun ceremony—Heaven crowned him.

sentences.zh: 祚逮朕躬，統承洪業。

translations.literal: The register reached Our person; We inherit the vast enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: The mandate passed to Mingdi himself.

sentences.zh: 蓋聞昔帝堯，元愷旣舉，凶族未流，登舜百揆，然後百揆時序，內平外成，授位明堂，退終天祿，故能冠德百王，表功高嶽。

translations.literal: We have heard that in antiquity Emperor Yao, once the Yuan and Kai were raised and evil clans had not yet been banished, he elevated Shun to director of all affairs—then the hundred duties had proper sequence; within was peace and without accomplishment; he yielded position in the Bright Hall and retired to end Heaven's stipend—therefore he could crown virtue above hundred kings and manifest merit higher than mountains.
translations.idiomatic: It praised Yao's abdication to Shun as the model of righteous transfer.

sentences.zh: 自往迄今，彌歷七代，歲曁三千，而大運來復，庸命底績，纂我民主，作建皇極。

translations.literal: From past to present it has spanned seven generations and three thousand years—yet the great mandate returns; obedient charge achieves merit; it renews Our people's ruler and establishes the imperial pivot.
translations.idiomatic: Seven cycles later Han's mandate returned to Wei.

sentences.zh: 念重光，紹咸池，繼韶夏，超羣后之遐蹤，邈商、周之慙德，可謂高朗令終，昭明洪烈之懿盛者矣。

translations.literal: Reflecting on doubled radiance, continuing Xianchi, handing on Shao and Xia, surpassing the distant tracks of former lords, transcending Shang and Zhou's ashamed virtue—this can be called a lofty and bright fine end, manifesting splendid mighty virtue's abundant greatness.
translations.idiomatic: It stacked mythical parallels to praise the abdication's perfection.

sentences.zh: 非夫漢、魏與天地合德，與四時合信，動和民神，格于上下，其孰能至於此乎？

translations.literal: Unless Han and Wei joined virtue with Heaven and earth and matched faith with the four seasons, moving in harmony with people and spirits and penetrating above and below—who could reach this?
translations.idiomatic: Who but a cosmic harmony of Han and Wei could achieve such virtue?

sentences.zh: 朕惟孝獻享年不永，欽若顧命，考之典謨，恭述皇考先靈遺意，闡崇弘謚，奉成聖美，以章希世同符之隆，以傳億載不朽之榮。

translations.literal: We reflect that Emperor Xiaoxian did not live many years; reverently obeying testamentary charge, examining the canonical models, respectfully narrating the departed August Father's intent, clarifying and enlarging the grand posthumous title, completing sagely beauty—thereby to manifest the rarity of a matching tally in the age and to transmit glory imperishable for hundred million years.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi framed the posthumous honors as fulfilling his father's pledge to Emperor Xian.

sentences.zh: 魂而有靈，嘉茲弘休。

translations.literal: If the soul has awareness, favor this grand blessing.
translations.idiomatic: May the spirit approve this bounty.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, alas how sorrowful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the ritual cry of mourning.

sentences.zh: 」八月壬申，葬于山陽國，陵曰禪陵，置園邑。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day renshen, he was buried in the Shanyang state; the mausoleum is called Shan Mausoleum; a garden and settlement were established.
translations.idiomatic: On eighth-month renshen he was buried at Shanling in Shanyang with an endowed tomb precinct.

sentences.zh: 葬之日，帝制錫衰弁絰，哭之慟。

translations.literal: On the day of burial the Emperor wore fine hemp mourning with cap cord and forehead band and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: At the funeral Mingdi donned tin-hemp mourning and wept as for a true parent.

sentences.zh: 適孫桂氏鄉侯康，嗣立爲山陽公。〉

translations.literal: The eldest grandson Duke Kang of Guishi township succeeded and was established as Duke of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: His heir's grandson, Marquis Kang of Guishi, succeeded as Duke of Shanyang."

sentences.zh: 是月，諸葛亮出斜谷，屯渭南，司馬宣王率諸軍拒之。

translations.literal: That month Zhuge Liang came out of Xie Valley, encamped south of the Wei River, and Sima Yi the Duke of Xuan led the armies to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang emerged from Xie Valley onto the Wei south bank; Sima Yi confronted him.

sentences.zh: 詔宣王：「但堅壁拒守以挫其鋒，彼進不得志，退無與戰，乆停則糧盡，虜略無所獲，則必走矣。

translations.literal: An edict told Sima Yi: "Only hold fast behind walls to blunt his edge; when he advances he cannot achieve his aim, when he retreats none will fight him—a long halt exhausts grain and plunder yields nothing—then he must flee.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered static defense: starve Zhuge Liang out, then chase him.

sentences.zh: 走而追之，以逸待勞，全勝之道也。」

translations.literal: When he flees pursue him—await labor with leisure—that is the way of complete victory."
translations.idiomatic: Strike him in retreat while your men are fresh—that is total victory."

sentences.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：亮旣屢遣使交書，又致巾幗婦人之飾，以怒宣王。

translations.literal: The Wei Shi Chunqiu states: Liang had repeatedly sent envoys with letters and also sent women's head-wrap ornaments to anger Sima Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Shi Chunqiu says Zhuge Liang taunted Sima Yi with letters and women's hats.

sentences.zh: 宣王將出戰，辛毗杖節奉詔，勒宣王及軍吏已下，乃止。

translations.literal: When Sima Yi was about to give battle, Xin Pi grasped the baton bearing an edict and restrained Sima Yi and all officers below—only then did they stop.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi tried to fight, Xin Pi arrived with an imperial staff and held him to the defensive.

sentences.zh: 宣王見亮使，唯問其寢食及其事之煩簡，不問戎事。

translations.literal: When Sima Yi saw Liang's envoy he only asked about his sleep and food and whether his duties were heavy or light—he did not ask about military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi asked Zhuge Liang's envoy only about diet and workload—not war.

sentences.zh: 使對曰：「諸葛公夙興夜寐，罰二十已上，皆親覽焉；

translations.literal: The envoy replied: "Lord Zhuge rises early and sleeps late; for punishments of twenty strokes or more he personally reviews each;
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said Zhuge Liang burned midnight oil and reviewed every flogging above twenty blows.

sentences.zh: 所啖食不過數升。

translations.literal: what he eats amounts to no more than several sheng per meal.
translations.idiomatic: He ate only a few sheng of grain a day.

sentences.zh: 」宣王曰：「亮體斃矣，其能久乎？」〉

translations.literal: Sima Yi said: "Liang's body is exhausted—how long can he endure?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi answered: "He is killing himself—how long can he last?"

sentences.zh: 五月，太白晝見。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Venus was visible by day.
translations.idiomatic: In May Venus appeared in daylight.

sentences.zh: 孫權入居巢湖口，向合肥新城，又遣將陸議、孫韶各將萬餘人入淮、沔。

translations.literal: Sun Quan moved into the mouth of Lake Chao and advanced on New Hefei; he also sent Lu Yi (Lu Xun) and Sun Shao each leading over ten thousand men into the Huai and Mian rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan threatened Hefei while Lu Xun and Sun Shao drove up the Huai.

sentences.zh: 六月，征東將軍滿寵進軍拒之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month General Who Subdues the East Man Chong advanced the army to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: In June Man Chong marched to meet him.

sentences.zh: 寵欲拔新城守，致賊壽春，帝不聽，曰：「昔漢光武遣兵縣據略陽，終以破隗囂，先帝東置合肥，南守襄陽，西固祁山，賊來輒破於三城之下者，地有所必爭也。

translations.literal: Chong wished to abandon New City's defense and lure the bandits to Shouchun—the Emperor did not consent and said: "Of old Emperor Guangwu of Han sent troops to seize Lüeyang and in the end defeated Wei Ao; the late Emperor set Hefei on the east, defended Xiangyang on the south, fortified Mount Qi on the west—whenever bandits came they were crushed below those three cities because those grounds had to be contested.
translations.idiomatic: Man Chong wanted to yield New Hefei to lure Wu inland; Mingdi refused, citing Guangwu's Lüeyang stratagem and Wei's triple fortress line.

sentences.zh: 縱權攻新城，必不能拔。

translations.literal: Even if Quan attacks New City he will certainly be unable to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan could not crack New Hefei even if he tried.

sentences.zh: 勑諸將堅守，吾將自往征之，比至，恐權走也。

translations.literal: Order the generals to hold firm—We shall personally go on campaign—by the time We arrive We fear Quan will already have fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the walls—Mingdi would sail east himself and expected Sun Quan to run.

sentences.zh: 」秋七月壬寅，帝親御龍舟東征，權攻新城，將軍張頴等拒守力戰，帝軍未至數百里，權遁走，議、韶等亦退。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, on day renyin, the Emperor personally commanded the dragon boat on an eastern campaign; Quan attacked New City; Generals Zhang Ying and others resisted and fought fiercely—the Emperor's army had not yet come within several hundred li when Quan fled; Lu Yi and Sun Shao also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On autumn renyin Mingdi took the dragon fleet east; Sun Quan fled before the imperial host neared, and Wu's generals followed.

sentences.zh: 羣臣以爲大將軍方與諸葛亮相持未解，車駕可西幸長安。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers thought the Grand General was still locked in stalemate with Zhuge Liang—the imperial carriage could travel west to favor Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers wanted the emperor to rush west to Zhuge Liang's front.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「權走，亮膽破，大將軍以制之，吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Quan has fled—Liang's courage is broken—the Grand General controls him—We have no worry.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi said Sun Quan's retreat left Zhuge Liang isolated—Sima Yi had him.

sentences.zh: 」遂進軍幸壽春，錄諸將功，封賞各有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced the army to favor Shouchun, recorded the generals' merit, and distributed enfeoffments and rewards by grade.
translations.idiomatic: He proceeded to Shouchun and handed out battle honors.

sentences.zh: 八月己未，大曜兵，饗六軍，遣使者持節犒勞合肥、壽春諸軍。

translations.literal: On day jiwei in the eighth month he greatly displayed troops, feasted the six armies, and sent envoys with insignia to reward the armies at Hefei and Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei he reviewed the armies and sent gifts to Hefei and Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，行還許昌宮。

translations.literal: On day xinsi he traveled in favor back to Xuchang palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the court returned to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 司馬宣王與亮相持，連圍積日，亮數挑戰，宣王堅壘不應。

translations.literal: Sima Yi and Liang stood off against each other, besieging one another many days in succession; Liang repeatedly challenged; Sima Yi held firm behind ramparts and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi refused Zhuge Liang's taunts and stayed entrenched.

sentences.zh: 會亮卒，其軍退還。

translations.literal: When Liang died his army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang's death broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙丑，月犯鎮星及軒轅。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, on day yichou, the moon trespassed Saturn and the Xuanyuan asterism.
translations.idiomatic: On winter yichou the moon passed Saturn and Xuanyuan.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，月犯太白。

translations.literal: On day wuyin the moon trespassed Venus.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the moon occulted Venus.

sentences.zh: 十一月，京都地震，從東南來，隱隱有聲，搖動屋瓦。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the capital was shaken by an earthquake coming from the southeast with a dull rumble that shifted roof tiles.
translations.idiomatic: November brought a southeast earthquake to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔有司刪定大辟，減死罪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he ordered the relevant offices to revise capital punishment statutes and reduce capital crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In December capital statutes were trimmed to spare more convicts.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月戊子，以大將軍司馬宣王爲太尉。

translations.literal: In the third year, spring, first month, on day wuzi, he appointed Grand General Sima Yi Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi in spring of the third year of Qinglong Sima Yi became grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 己亥，復置朔方郡。

translations.literal: On day jihai he re-established Shuofang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Shuofang commandery was revived.

sentences.zh: 京都大疫。

translations.literal: A great plague struck the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Plague ravaged Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，皇太后崩。

translations.literal: On day dingsi the Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Empress Dowager Guo died.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，隕石于壽光縣。

translations.literal: On day yihai a meteorite fell in Shouguang county.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai a meteorite struck Shouguang.

sentences.zh: 三月庚寅，葬文德郭后，營陵于首陽陵澗西，如終制。

translations.literal: On day gengyin in the third month he buried Empress Wende Lady Guo and built her tomb west of the Shouyang ridge ravine according to her final instructions.
translations.idiomatic: In third-month gengyin Lady Guo was buried west of Shouyang per her modest burial wishes.

sentences.zh: 〈顧愷之《啟蒙注》曰：魏時人有開周王冢者，得殉葬女子，經數日而有氣，數月而能語；

translations.literal: Gu Kaizhi's Qimeng Zhu states: In Wei times someone opened the Zhou king's tomb and obtained a buried woman; after several days she drew breath; after months she could speak.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Kaizhi tells of a woman revived from an ancient Zhou tomb.

sentences.zh: 年可二十。

translations.literal: Her age was about twenty.
translations.idiomatic: She looked about twenty.

sentences.zh: 送詣京師，郭太后愛養之。

translations.literal: They sent her to the capital; Empress Dowager Guo loved and raised her.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Guo adopted her at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十餘年，太后崩，哀思哭泣，一年餘而死。〉

translations.literal: After more than ten years the Empress Dowager died; she wept in sorrow and after a year plus died.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager died a decade later, the girl grieved herself to death within a year."

sentences.zh: 是時，大治洛陽宮，起昭陽、太極殿，築緫章觀。

translations.literal: At this time he greatly built out the Luoyang palace, raising the Zhaoyang and Taiji halls and constructing the Zongzhang Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's palace sprouted Zhaoyang, Taiji, and the Zongzhang viewing tower.

sentences.zh: 百姓失農時，直臣楊阜、高堂隆等各數切諫，雖不能聽，常優容之。

translations.literal: Common people missed the farming season; straight ministers Yang Fu, Gaotang Long, and others each repeatedly remonstrated sharply—though he could not heed them, he often treated them with indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Palace labor stole the sowing season; Yang Fu and Gaotang Long protested relentlessly—Mingdi heard them out politely if not obediently.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：是年起太極諸殿，築緫章觀，高十餘丈，建翔鳳於其上；

translations.literal: The Wei Lue states: That year they raised the Taiji halls and built the Zongzhang Observatory, over ten zhang high, erecting a soaring phoenix atop it;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Lue describes Taiji and a ten-zhang Zongzhang tower topped by a phoenix.

sentences.zh: 又於芳林園中起陂池，楫櫂越歌；

translations.literal: also in Fanglin Garden they dug ponds—for oarsmen singing Yue songs;
translations.idiomatic: Fanglin Garden gained pools for boating and song.

sentences.zh: 又於列殿之北立八坊，諸才人以次序處其中，貴人夫人以上轉南附焉，其秩石擬百官之數。

translations.literal: also north of the row of halls they established eight wards—the talented ladies were lodged in order by rank; noble ladies and above moved south to adjoin them; their salary grades paralleled the officials' numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Eight courts housed ranked concubines whose stipends mirrored the civil list.

sentences.zh: 帝常游宴在內，乃選女子知書可付信者六人，以爲女尚書，使典省外奏事，處當畫可，自貴人以下至尚保，及給掖庭灑掃，習伎歌者，各有千數。

translations.literal: The Emperor often feasted inside; he then selected six literate women he could trust as female secretaries to manage outside memorials from the palace, to settle and approve with brush; from noble ladies down to attendants, palace sweepers, and trained singers—each category numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He ran the court from the harem—six female clerks vetted memorials while thousands of attendants filled the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 通引穀水過九龍殿前，爲玉井綺欄，蟾蜍含受，神龍吐出。

translations.literal: They diverted the Gu River past the Jiulong Hall, making jade wells with carved balustrades, toads receiving water and divine dragons spouting it.
translations.idiomatic: They plumbed the Gu past Jiulong Hall with jade-faced wells and bronze dragon fountains.

sentences.zh: 使博士馬均作司南車，水轉百戲。

translations.literal: He ordered Erudite Ma Jun to construct a south-pointing carriage and water-driven mechanical entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jun built a south-pointing carriage and water-powered automata.

sentences.zh: 歲首建巨獸，魚龍曼延，弄馬倒騎，備如漢西京之制，築閶闔諸門闕外罘罳。

translations.literal: At the new year they erected giant beasts, fish-and-dragon processions, trick riding and inverted riding—all like the Han western capital system—and built screen walls outside the Changhe gate towers.
translations.idiomatic: New Year's shows aped Western Han pageantry; screens rose outside Changhe Gate.

sentences.zh: 太子舍人張茂以吳、蜀數動，諸將出征，而帝盛興宮室，留意於玩飾，賜與無度，帑藏空竭；

translations.literal: Heir Attendant Zhang Mao, because Wu and Shu stirred repeatedly while generals campaigned, yet the Emperor greatly raised palace buildings and fixed attention on playthings, granting without measure until treasury and storehouses were exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao noted wars abroad while Mingdi poured the treasury into ornament.

sentences.zh: 又錄奪士女前已嫁爲吏民妻者，還以配士，旣聽以生口自贖，又簡選其有姿首者內之掖庭，乃上書諫曰：「臣伏見詔書，諸士女嫁非士者，一切錄奪，以配戰士，斯誠權時之宜，然非大化之善者也。

translations.literal: also registering gentlewomen already married to clerks and commoners and returning them to assign to soldiers—having permitted ransom with captives of matching age, yet also selecting the fair ones for the Rear Palace—thereupon he memorialized: "Your servant humbly sees the edict—all gentlewomen married to non-gentlemen are altogether registered and seized to match warriors—this is indeed expedient for the moment yet not the best of great transformation.
translations.idiomatic: He condemned seizing wives for soldiers—calling it expedient but unjust."

sentences.zh: 臣請論之。

translations.literal: Your servant requests to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to explain.

sentences.zh: 陛下，天之子也，百姓吏民，亦陛下之子也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is Heaven's son; the hundred surnames and clerks are also Your Majesty's sons.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and his people were equally sons of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 禮，賜君子小人不同日，所以殊貴賤也。

translations.literal: By ritual, gentlemen and petty men are not gifted on the same day—thereby distinguishing noble and base.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual separates gifts to nobles and commoners.

sentences.zh: 吏屬君子，士爲小人，今奪彼以與此，亦無以異於奪兄之妻妻弟也，於父母之恩偏矣。

translations.literal: Clerks belong among gentlemen; soldiers are petty men—now seizing from those to give to these differs in no way from seizing an elder brother's wife to marry a younger brother—the kindness toward parents is uneven.
translations.idiomatic: Moving clerks' wives to soldiers was like stealing a brother's bride—it skewed parental fairness.

sentences.zh: 又詔書聽得以生口年紀、顏色與妻相當者自代，故富者則傾家盡產，貧者舉假貸貰，貴買生口以贖其妻；

translations.literal: Further the edict permits replacing with living captives matching the wife's age and appearance—therefore the rich exhaust house and estate, the poor borrow on pledge and borrow dear—buying captives at high price to ransom their wives;
translations.idiomatic: Ransom rules beggared households buying stand-in slaves.

sentences.zh: 縣官以配士爲名而實內之掖庭，其醜惡者乃出與士。

translations.literal: the county office under the name of matching to soldiers in truth sends them into the Rear Palace—the ugly ones alone go to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Officials skimmed beauties for the harem and foisted plain women on the troops.

sentences.zh: 得婦者未必有懽心，而失妻者必有憂色，或窮或愁，皆不得志。

translations.literal: Those who gain wives need not feel joy and those who lose wives must wear sorrow—whether destitute or grieving, none achieve their desire.
translations.idiomatic: Neither new husbands nor robbed husbands ended content.

sentences.zh: 夫君有天下而不得萬姓之懽心者，尠不危殆。

translations.literal: Now a lord who possesses all under heaven yet cannot win the myriad households' joy rarely avoids danger.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who forfeits popular goodwill courts ruin.

sentences.zh: 且軍師在外數千萬人，一日之費非徒千金，舉天下之賦以奉此役，猶將不給，況復有宮庭非員無錄之女，椒房母后之家賞賜橫興，內外交引，其費半軍。

translations.literal: Moreover the armies abroad number tens of millions—a single day's expense is not merely a thousand in gold; raising all under heaven's taxes to supply this campaign still verges on insufficient—how much more when inner palace supernumerary women without roster multiply, when empress kin grant gifts wantonly, inner and outer bleeding each other—the expense equals half the army.
translations.idiomatic: Field armies drained the treasury—harem excess and consort clans cost half as much again.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝好神仙，信方士，掘地爲海，封土爲山，賴是時天下爲一，莫敢與爭者耳。

translations.literal: Of old Emperor Wu of Han loved immortality and trusted fangshi—he dug earth into seas and heaped earth into mountains—only because at that time all under heaven was one and none dared contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi's extravagance worked only in a unified empire.

sentences.zh: 自衰亂以來，四五十載，馬不捨鞍，士不釋甲，每一交戰，血流丹野，創痍號痛之聲于今未已。

translations.literal: Since decline and turmoil forty or fifty years—horses have not left saddles, men have not doffed armor—each time armies clash blood dyes the red fields; the sound of wounds and wailing has not ceased until today.
translations.idiomatic: Forty years of war had left Wei's people bleeding and weary.

sentences.zh: 猶彊寇在疆，圖危魏室。

translations.literal: Strong foes still lie on the borders plotting danger to the Wei house.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu still threatened the throne.

sentences.zh: 陛下不兢兢業業，念崇節約，思所以安天下者，而乃奢靡是務，中尚方純作玩弄之物，炫燿後園，建承露之盤，斯誠快耳目之觀，然亦足以騁寇讎之心矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not tread carefully in fear, thinking to honor thrift and pondering how to pacify all under heaven—instead You make extravagance Your task; the Inner Palace Workshop purely manufactures playthings to dazzle the rear garden and erect dew-catching trays—this indeed pleases eyes and ears—yet it is enough to hearten enemy hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi chased luxury while foes watched—vanity armed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 惜乎，舍堯舜之節儉，而爲漢武之侈事，臣竊爲陛下不取也。

translations.literal: Alas—to discard Yao and Shun's thrift for Emperor Wu of Han's excesses—your servant privately considers unworthy for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing Han Wudi over Yao's austerity was a mistake.

sentences.zh: 願陛下沛然下詔，萬幾之事有無益而有損者悉除去之，以所除無益之費，厚賜將士父母妻子之飢寒者，問民所疾而除其所惡，實倉廩，繕甲兵，恪恭以臨天下。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty freely issue an edict: of myriad affairs whatever lacks benefit yet brings harm—remove it all; use what was removed from useless expense to enrich soldiers' cold and hungry parents, wives, and children; inquire what afflicts the people and remove what they hate; fill granaries; repair armor and weapons; approach all under heaven with reverent respect.
translations.idiomatic: Cut waste, feed soldiers' families, fill granaries, mend arms—that was his remedy.

sentences.zh: 如是，吳賊面縛，蜀虜輿櫬，不待誅而自服，太平之路可計日而待也。

translations.literal: If so, Wu bandits will bind their own wrists and Shu captives will bear coffins on their backs—without awaiting execution they will submit of themselves—the road to great peace may wait counted days.
translations.idiomatic: Spend rightly and Wu and Shu would surrender without another battle.

sentences.zh: 陛下可無勞神思於海表，軍師高枕，戰士備員。

translations.literal: Your Majesty may spare divine thought beyond the seas—the armies pillow high and warriors stand in reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Wise rule would let generals rest.

sentences.zh: 今羣公皆結舌，而臣所以不敢不獻瞽言者，臣昔上要言，散騎奏臣書，以聽諫篇爲善，詔曰：『是也』，擢臣爲太子舍人；

translations.literal: Now the assembled dukes all seal their tongues—why your servant dares not withhold blind speech: your servant once submitted a bold memorial; Irregular Cavalry presented it; praising the chapter on accepting remonstrance—an edict said 'correct' and promoted your servant Heir Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao cited his earlier promotion for frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 且臣作書譏爲人臣不能諫諍，今有可諫之事而臣不諫，此爲作書虛妄而不能言也。

translations.literal: Moreover your servant composed a book mocking ministers unable to remonstrate—now there is matter for remonstrance yet your servant does not remonstrate—this makes the writing empty and proves inability to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Silence now would brand his own essays hypocrisy.

sentences.zh: 臣年五十，常恐至死無以報國，是以投軀沒身，冒昧以聞，惟陛下裁察。

translations.literal: Your servant is fifty years old and constantly fears dying without repaying the state—therefore casts aside body and risks offense to inform—only Your Majesty judges.
translations.idiomatic: At fifty he feared dying disloyal if he stayed mute.

sentences.zh: 」書通，上顧左右曰：「張茂恃鄉里故也。

translations.literal: When the memorial had passed through, the Emperor looked to left and right and said, "Zhang Mao relies on fellow-townsmen ties.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi sniffed that Zhang Mao traded on local connections.

sentences.zh: 」以事付散騎而已。

translations.literal: He handed the matter to Irregular Cavalry only.
translations.idiomatic: He routed it to petty bureaucrats and forgot it.

sentences.zh: 茂字彥林，沛人。〉

translations.literal: Mao's courtesy name was Yanlin; he was a man of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao, courtesy Yanlin, was a native of Pei."

sentences.zh: 秋七月，洛陽崇華殿災，八月庚午，立皇子芳爲齊王，詢爲秦王。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, Chonghua Hall in Luoyang burned; on day gengwu in the eighth month he established the imperial sons Fang as Prince of Qi and Xun as Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: After Chonghua burned, on gengwu he named Princes Fang and Xun of Qi and Qin.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，行還洛陽宮。

translations.literal: On day dingsi he traveled in favor back to Luoyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the court returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 命有司復崇華，改名九龍殿。

translations.literal: He ordered the relevant offices to rebuild Chonghua and renamed it Jiulong Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua rose again as Jiulong Hall.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己酉，中山王衮薨。

translations.literal: On day jiyou in winter, tenth month, Prince Gun of Zhongshan died.
translations.idiomatic: On winter jiyou Prince Gun of Zhongshan died.

sentences.zh: 壬申，太白晝見。

translations.literal: On day renshen Venus was visible by day.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Venus shone at noon.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁酉，行幸許昌宮。

translations.literal: On day dingyou in the eleventh month he traveled in favor to Xuchang palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou in November he moved court to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：是歲張掖郡刪丹縣金山玄川溢涌，寶石負圖，狀象靈龜，廣一丈六尺，長一丈七尺一寸，圍五丈八寸，立于川西。

translations.literal: The Wei Shi Chunqiu states: That year in Zhangye commandery's Shandan county the Golden River of Mysterious Water welled and overflowed; a precious stone bore a diagram shaped like a spirit tortoise—one zhang six chi wide, one zhang seven chi one cun long, five zhang eight cun in girth—standing west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: A Zhangye flood allegedly revealed a tortoise-shaped chart stone.

sentences.zh: 有石馬七，其一仙人騎之，其一羈絆，其五有形而不善成。

translations.literal: There were seven stone horses—one ridden by an immortal—one bridled—five having form but not well finished.
translations.idiomatic: Seven stone horses—some riders, some unfinished.

sentences.zh: 有玉匣關蓋於前，上有玉字，玉玦二，璜一。

translations.literal: There was a jade casket with lid before it; on top were jade characters; two jade pendants and one huang.
translations.idiomatic: Jade fittings and inscriptions surrounded it.

sentences.zh: 麒麟在東，鳳鳥在南，白虎在西，犧牛在北，馬自中布列四面，色皆蒼白。

translations.literal: The qilin was east, the phoenix south, the white tiger west, the sacrificial ox north; horses spread from the center to the four sides—all pale blue-white.
translations.idiomatic: Carvings placed omens on four sides—azure beasts and horses.

sentences.zh: 其南有五字，曰「上上三天王」；

translations.literal: On its south were five characters saying 'Supreme Supreme Three Heaven Kings';
translations.idiomatic: One legend read 'Highest Three Heaven Kings.'

sentences.zh: 又曰「述大金，大討曹，金但取之，金立中，大金馬一匹在中，大吉開壽，此馬甲寅述水」。

translations.literal: it also said 'Transmit great metal—great punish Cao—metal only take it—metal stands in center—great golden horse one in center—great auspicious open longevity—this horse jiayin transmit water'.
translations.idiomatic: Another prophetic string promised Wei would fall to 'great metal'—catering to Jin propaganda.

sentences.zh: 凡「中」字六，「金」字十；

translations.literal: In all there were six 'center' characters and ten 'metal' characters;
translations.idiomatic: The omens stacked 'center' and 'metal' glyphs.

sentences.zh: 又有若八卦及列宿孛彗之象焉。

translations.literal: there were also figures like the eight trigrams and asterisms and comets.
translations.idiomatic: Shapes echoed trigrams and constellations.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：又有一雞象。

translations.literal: The Shi Yu states: There was also a chicken image.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi Yu adds a rooster carving.

sentences.zh: 《搜神記》曰：初，漢元、成之世，先識之士有言曰，魏年有和，當有開石於西三千餘里，繫五馬，文曰「大討曹」。

translations.literal: The Soushen Ji states: At the beginning of the Han Yuandi-Chengdi era a foreknowing gentleman said: In Wei years there will be harmony—there should be a stone opening three thousand li to the west—tying five horses—inscription 'great punish Cao'.
translations.idiomatic: Han scholars allegedly predicted a 'punish Cao' stone in the west.

sentences.zh: 及魏之初興也，張掖之柳谷，有開石焉，始見於建安，形成於黃初，文備於太和，周圍七尋，中高一仞，蒼質素章，龍馬、麟鹿、鳳皇、仙人之象，粲然咸著，此一事者，魏、晉代興之符也。

translations.literal: When Wei first rose, in Zhangye's Willow Valley there was an opening stone—first seen in Jian'an, formed in Huangchu, text complete in Taihe—circumference seven xun, center one ren high—green quality, white pattern—dragon-horse, qilin-deer, phoenix, immortal images—brilliantly all manifest—this one matter is the talisman of Wei and Jin dynastic rise.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi ties Willow Valley stones from Jian'an through Taihe to Wei-Jin legitimacy.

sentences.zh: 至晉泰始三年，張掖太守焦勝上言，以留郡本國圖校今石文，文字多少不同，謹具圖上。

translations.literal: By Jin Taishi 3 Zhangye prefect Jiao Sheng memorialized, comparing the present stone text with the old commandery map—the characters differed in number—he respectfully submitted the diagram.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 3 Jiao Sheng re-measured the glyphs against older rubbings.

sentences.zh: 桉其文有五馬象，其一有人平上幘，執戟而乘之，其一有若馬形而不成，其字有「金」，有「中」，有「大司馬」，有「王」，有「大吉」，有「正」，有「開壽」，其一成行，曰「金當取之」。

translations.literal: Examining its text there were five horse images—one person in flat cap holding ji riding—one like a horse shape but incomplete—its characters had 'metal,' 'center,' 'grand marshal,' 'king,' 'great auspicious,' 'correct,' 'open longevity'—one line reading 'metal ought take it'.
translations.idiomatic: The cracks promised Jin ('metal') would supplant Wei.

sentences.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：氐池縣大柳谷口夜激波涌溢，其聲如雷，曉而有蒼石立水中，長一丈六尺，高八尺，白石畫之，爲十三馬，一牛，一鳥，八卦玉玦之象，皆隆起，其文曰「大討曹，適水中，甲寅」。

translations.literal: The Han Jin Chunqiu states: At Dichi county's great willow valley mouth waves surged by night with sound like thunder; at dawn a pale stone stood in the water—one zhang six chi long, eight chi high—white stone drew thirteen horses, one ox, one bird, eight trigrams and jade pendant images—all raised—its text said 'great punish Cao—fit in water—jiayin'.
translations.idiomatic: Another flood tale etched 'punish Cao' on a river stone.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其「討」也，使鑿去爲「計」，以蒼石窒之，宿昔而白石滿焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor hated the character 'punish' and had it chiseled into 'calculate'; he blocked it with green stone—overnight white stones filled it.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi had 'punish' carved to 'calculate' and buried the omen—stones multiplied overnight in legend.

sentences.zh: 至晉初，其文愈明，馬象皆煥徹如玉焉。〉

translations.literal: By the Jin inception the text grew clearer and the horse images all gleamed translucent as jade.
translations.idiomatic: By Western Jin the omens supposedly shone like jade."

sentences.zh: 四年春二月，太白復晝見，月犯太白，又犯軒轅一星，入太微而出。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, spring, second month, Venus again appeared by day; the moon trespassed Venus and also trespassed one star of Xuanyuan; it entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure and exited.
translations.idiomatic: Spring omens: Venus by day, lunar occultations, and entry into Taiwei.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，置崇文觀，徵善屬文者以充之。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, he established the Chongwen Observatory and summoned those skilled at composition to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: Summer founded Chongwen Hall for literati.

sentences.zh: 五月乙卯，司徒董昭薨。

translations.literal: On day yimao in the fifth month Minister of Education Dong Zhao died.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in May Dong Zhao died.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，肅慎氏獻楛矢。

translations.literal: On day dingsi the Sushen tribe presented mulberry-arrow shafts.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Sushen envoys brought birch-bark arrows.

sentences.zh: 六月壬申，詔曰：「有虞氏畫象而民弗犯，周人刑錯而不用。

translations.literal: On day renshen in the sixth month an edict stated: "The You Yu clan painted images and the people did not offend; the Zhou people set punishments aside and did not use them.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen an edict invoked Yu's pictorial laws and Zhou's unused punishments."

sentences.zh: 朕從百王之末，追望上世之風，邈乎何相去之遠？

translations.literal: We follow after the hundred kings' last generation, gazing back at high antiquity's ways—how vast the distance between!
translations.idiomatic: Living after late kings, Mingdi mourned how far his justice fell short of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 法令滋章，犯者彌多，刑罰愈衆，而姦不可止。

translations.literal: Statutes grow ever more detailed—offenders increase—punishments multiply—yet wickedness cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: More laws bred more crime—punishment multiplied without ending fraud.

sentences.zh: 往者桉大辟之條，多所蠲除，思濟生民之命，此朕之至意也。

translations.literal: In the past We examined capital-crime clauses and removed much, intending to aid the people's lives—this is Our utmost intent.
translations.idiomatic: He had already eased capital statutes to spare lives.

sentences.zh: 而郡國斃獄，一歲之中尚過數百，豈朕訓導不醇，俾民輕罪，將苛法猶存，爲之陷穽乎？

translations.literal: Yet commandery and kingdom prisons still exceed several hundred deaths in one year—is it that Our instruction is not pure, leading the people to slight crimes—do harsh laws still remain as traps for them?
translations.idiomatic: Yet hundreds still died in jail yearly—was teaching weak or the law still a snare?

sentences.zh: 有司其議獄緩死，務從寬簡，及乞恩者，或辭未出而獄以報斷，非所以究理盡情也。

translations.literal: Let the relevant offices deliberate delaying execution for capital cases, striving for leniency and simplicity; as for those begging grace—sometimes their plea has not yet emerged yet the prison already reports sentence passed—this is not the way to exhaust principle and fully express feeling.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered reviews before execution so mercy pleas could reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 其令廷尉及天下獄官，諸有死罪具獄以定，非謀反及手殺人，亟語其親治，有乞恩者，使與奏當文書俱上，朕將思所以全之。

translations.literal: Let it be ordered that the Commandant of Justice and prison officials throughout the realm—for all capital cases with complete files determined—unless rebellion or hands-on murder—swiftly inform their kin to manage matters; where there are grace seekers, let them submit together with the verdict memorial—We will ponder how to spare them.
translations.idiomatic: Death sentences needed kin notified and clemency petitions bundled with court findings—except treason and murder.

sentences.zh: 其布告天下，使明朕意。」

translations.literal: Let it be proclaimed all under heaven to clarify Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was published empire-wide."

sentences.zh: 景初元年春正月壬辰，山茌縣言黃龍見。

translations.literal: In Jingchu 1, spring, first month, on day renchen, Shanzhi county reported a yellow dragon appeared.
translations.idiomatic: On Jingchu renchen Shanzhi reported a yellow dragon omen.

sentences.zh: 〈茌音仕狸反。〉

translations.literal: Chi is read shi-li fan (phonetic note).
translations.idiomatic: Phonetic gloss for the place-name character (fanqie: shi plus li).

sentences.zh: 於是有司奏，以爲魏得地統，宜以建丑之月爲正。

translations.literal: Thereupon the relevant offices memorialized, considering that Wei obtained the earth's correspondence and ought to take the month jianchou as first month.
translations.idiomatic: Officials argued Wei held 'earth' phase and should begin the year in jianchou (twelfth month).

sentences.zh: 三月，定歷改年爲孟夏四月。

translations.literal: In the third month they fixed the calendar and changed the year so the old fourth month became first month of summer.
translations.idiomatic: They reset the calendar so summer's first month opened the year.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：初，文皇帝即位，以受禪于漢，因循漢正朔弗改。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu states: At first when Emperor Wen assumed the throne, because he had received abdication from Han, he followed Han's calendar without change.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi had kept Han's calendar after abdication.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮著論，以爲五帝三王雖同氣共祖，禮不相襲，正朔自宜改變，以明受命之運。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was Heir Apparent he composed a treatise holding that although the Five Emperors and Three Kings shared breath and common ancestry, ritual does not repeat itself—the first month ought to change to clarify the movement of received mandate.
translations.idiomatic: As heir Mingdi had already argued new dynasties need new calendars.

sentences.zh: 及即位，優游者久之，史官復著言宜改，乃詔三公、特進、九卿、中郎將、大夫、博士、議郎、千石、六百石博議，議者或不同。

translations.literal: When he mounted the throne he hesitated long; the historians again wrote that change was fitting—thereupon he ordered the three dukes, special advance, nine ministers, general of the Gentlemen of the Household, grandees, erudites, deliberation gentlemen, thousand-shi and six-hundred-shi officials to debate broadly—those who debated sometimes differed.
translations.idiomatic: He stalled until scholars renewed the debate with divided opinions.

sentences.zh: 帝據古典，甲子詔曰：「夫太極運三辰五星於上，元氣轉三統五行於下，登降周旋，終則又始。

translations.literal: He relied on classical antiquity; on jiazi day an edict stated: "The Grand Ultimate moves the three luminaries and five planets above; primordial breath turns the three systems and five phases below—ascending, descending, circling—when ended then again beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The edict invoked cosmology—celestial wheels and five-element cycles.

sentences.zh: 故仲尼作春秋，於三微之月，每月稱王，以明三正迭相爲首。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhongni composed the Spring and Autumn Annals—in the three subtle months he each month styled 'king' to clarify the three first months succeeding one another as head.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius' Annals honored three competing calendar starts.

sentences.zh: 今推三統之次，魏得地統，當以建丑之月爲正月。

translations.literal: Now pushing the sequence of the three systems—Wei obtained the earth system—it ought to take the jianchou month as first month.
translations.idiomatic: Wei matched the earth 'tong'—year must begin in jianchou.

sentences.zh: 考之羣藝，厥義章矣。

translations.literal: Examining the collected classics—the meaning is manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Canon backed the reform.

sentences.zh: 其改青龍五年三月爲景初元年四月。」〉

translations.literal: Let Qinglong 5 third month be changed to Jingchu 1 fourth month."
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 5 month 3 became Jingchu 1 month 4."

sentences.zh: 服色尚黃，犧牲用白，戎事乘黑首白馬，建大赤之旂，朝會建大白之旗。

translations.literal: Dress color esteemed yellow; sacrifices used white victims; for military affairs ride black-maned white horses; raise great scarlet banners at court; at assemblies raise great white banners.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress yellow, victims white, war horses black-maned white, banners scarlet for court and white for martial display.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之桉：魏爲土行，故服色尚黃。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi submits: Wei is earth phase—therefore dress esteems yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Pei notes earth element dictated yellow robes.

sentences.zh: 行殷之時，以建丑爲正，故犧牲旂旗一用殷禮。

translations.literal: In Yin times they took jianchou as correct—therefore victims and banners wholly followed Yin ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Animal and banner colors followed Yin precedent under jianchou.

sentences.zh: 禮記云：「夏后氏尚黑，故戎事乘驪，牲用玄；

translations.literal: The Record of Rites states: "The Xia dynasty esteemed black—therefore military affairs rode black horses and victims used dark blood;
translations.idiomatic: Rites quote Xia favoring black mounts.

sentences.zh: 殷人尚白，戎事乘翰，牲用白；

translations.literal: the Yin people esteemed white—military affairs rode pale horses and victims used white;
translations.idiomatic: Yin favored white horses and white victims.

sentences.zh: 周人尚赤，戎事乘騵，牲用騂。

translations.literal: the Zhou people esteemed scarlet—military affairs rode bay horses with yellow eyes and victims used red-yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou preferred sorrel mounts and chestnut victims.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄云：「夏后氏以建寅爲正，物生色黑；

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan states: "The Xia took jianyin as correct—things' born color is black;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explains color-phase tie to month stem.

sentences.zh: 殷以建丑爲正，物牙色白；

translations.literal: Yin took jianchou as correct—things' sprouting color is white;
translations.idiomatic: Yin's white matched sprouting under jianchou.

sentences.zh: 周以建子爲正，物萌色赤。

translations.literal: Zhou took jianzi as correct—things' budding color is scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's red matched buds under jianzi.

sentences.zh: 翰，白色馬也，易曰『白馬翰如』。

translations.literal: Han means pale horses—the Changes says 'white horses hoof-high.'"
translations.idiomatic: 'Han' glosses as white—the Zhou Yi cites white horses.

sentences.zh: 」周禮巾車職「建大赤以朝」，大白以即戎，此則周以正色之旗以朝，先代之旗即戎。

translations.literal: The Zhou li Director of Chariots' duty: 'Raise great scarlet for court'—great white for going to war—thus Zhou used orthodox-color banner at court and former dynasties' banner for war.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou li distinguished audience banners from campaign banners.

sentences.zh: 今魏用殷禮，變周之制，故建大白以朝，大赤即戎。〉

translations.literal: Now Wei uses Yin ritual, altering Zhou's system—therefore raises great white at court and great scarlet for war.
translations.idiomatic: Wei inverted Zhou: white at peace, scarlet in war—per Yin."

sentences.zh: 改

translations.literal: Change
translations.idiomatic: [Calendar heading:] Amendment.

sentences.zh: 〈大和歷〉

translations.literal: Dahe calendar
translations.idiomatic: From the Dahe calendar treatise.

sentences.zh: 曰

translations.literal: states
translations.idiomatic: It reads

sentences.zh: 〈景初歷〉

translations.literal: Jingchu calendar
translations.idiomatic: to the Jingchu calendar treatise.
End of calendar citation.

sentences.zh: 其春夏秋冬孟仲季月雖與正歲不同，至於郊祀、迎氣、礿祠、蒸甞、巡狩、蒐田、分至啟閉、班宣時令、中氣早晚、敬授民事，皆以正歲斗建爲歷數之序。

translations.literal: Although its spring, summer, autumn, winter, first, middle, and last months differ from the orthodox year's reckoning—as for suburban sacrifice, welcoming qi, spring and autumn temple offerings, winter and summer offerings, imperial tours, hunt reviews, solstices and solar terms, quarter seasons, promulgating seasonal orders, mid-term qi early or late, reverently granting people their tasks—all take the orthodox year's dipper establishment as the sequence of calendrical reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal rites still tracked the old dipper month despite civil date shift.

sentences.zh: 五月己巳，行還洛陽宮。

translations.literal: On day jisi in the fifth month he traveled in favor back to Luoyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi in May the court returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 己丑，大赦。

translations.literal: On day jichou a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou came amnesty.

sentences.zh: 六月戊申，京都地震。

translations.literal: On day wushen in the sixth month the capital was shaken by earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On sixth-month wushen Luoyang quaked.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以尚書令陳矯爲司徒，尚書右僕射衞臻爲司空。

translations.literal: On day jihai he appointed Minister Director Chen Jiao Minister of Education and Minister of the Right Wei Zhen Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Chen Jiao became minister of education and Wei Zhen minister of works.

sentences.zh: 丁未，分魏興之魏陽、錫郡之安富、上庸爲上庸郡。

translations.literal: On day dingwei he divided Weiyang of Weixing, Anfu of Xi commandery, and Shangyong to form Shangyong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei new Shangyong commandery was carved from three counties.

sentences.zh: 省錫郡，以錫縣屬魏興郡。

translations.literal: He abolished Xi commandery and attached Xi county to Weixing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xi commandery was folded and its seat joined Weixing.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：武皇帝撥亂反正，爲魏太祖，樂用武始之舞。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: Emperor Wu set chaos aright and became Wei Taizu—music uses the Wushi dance.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's temple music was Wushi.

sentences.zh: 文皇帝應天受命，爲魏高祖，樂用咸熙之舞。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen answered Heaven's charge and became Wei Gaozu—music uses the Xianxi dance.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi's shrine used Xianxi.

sentences.zh: 帝制作興治，爲魏烈祖，樂用章武之舞。

translations.literal: The Emperor fashioned institutions and raised order—becoming Wei Liezu—music uses the Zhangwu dance.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi claimed Liezu with Zhangwu choreography.

sentences.zh: 三祖之廟萬世不毀，其餘四廟親盡迭毀，如周后稷、文、武廟祧之制。

translations.literal: The three ancestors' temples shall never be destroyed through the ages; the remaining four temples when kinship ties are exhausted shall rotate destruction—like Zhou's system for Houji, Wen, and Wu distant shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Three eternal shrines plus rotating four—mirroring Zhou geneology rules.

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛曰：夫謚以表行，廟以存容，皆於旣沒然後著焉，所以原始要終，以示百世也。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: Posthumous titles display conduct; temples preserve likeness—both attach only after death so one may trace beginning and end and display them to hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng scolds premature temple honors.

sentences.zh: 未有當年而逆制祖宗，未終而豫自尊顯。

translations.literal: Never has one in his own lifetime reverse-fashioned ancestors; never before the end presumptuously elevated himself.
translations.idiomatic: Living rulers should not name themselves founding ancestors.

sentences.zh: 昔華樂以厚斂致譏，周人以豫凶違禮，魏之羣司，於是乎失正。〉

translations.literal: Of old Hua Le earned ridicule for heavy levies; Zhou men violated ritual by preparing mourning gear early—Wei's officers here lost correctness."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng compares Mingdi to notorious precedents of vanity."

sentences.zh: 詔青、兖、幽、冀四州大作海船。

translations.literal: He ordered Qing, Yan, You, and Ji four commanderies to build large sea ships on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Four northern provinces mass-produced war junks.

sentences.zh: 九月，冀、兖、徐、豫四州民遇水，遣侍御史循行沒溺死亡及失財產者，在所開倉振救之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the people of Ji, Yan, Xu, and Yu commanderies met flooding; he dispatched attendants censors to tour and examine drowned dead and those who lost property; wherever they were, open granaries and relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: September floods brought imperial grain relief.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，皇后毛氏卒。

translations.literal: On day gengchen Empress Mao died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Empress Mao passed away.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁未，月犯熒惑。

translations.literal: On day dingwei in winter, tenth month, the moon trespassed Mars.
translations.idiomatic: On winter dingwei the moon occulted Mars.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，葬悼毛后于愍陵。

translations.literal: On day guichou he buried Empress Dao Mao at Min Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Lady Mao was buried at Minling.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，營洛陽南委粟山爲圜丘。

translations.literal: On day yimao he worked Mount Weisu south of Luoyang into a round-altar mound.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao he shaped southern Weisu hill into Heaven's round altar.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》載詔曰：「蓋帝王受命，莫不恭承天地以章神明，尊祀世統以昭功德，故先代之典旣著，則禘郊祖宗之制備也。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu records an edict: "Emperors receiving mandate all reverently inherit Heaven and earth to manifest spirits; honor sacrificial succession to display merit—therefore former dynasties' canons once fixed, the suburban and ancestral temple system is complete.
translations.idiomatic: An edict framed suburban sacrifice reform.

sentences.zh: 昔漢氏之初，承秦滅學之後，采摭殘缺，以備郊祀，自甘泉后土、雍宮五畤，神祇兆位，多不見經，是以制度無常，一彼一此，四百餘年，廢無禘祀。

translations.literal: At Han's beginning, inheriting Qin's destruction of learning, they gathered fragments to supply suburban sacrifice—from Ganquan and Hou soil, Yong palace's five shrines—spirit positions mostly lack canonical warrant—therefore institutions lacked constancy, now this now that—more than four hundred years without di sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Han sacrifices had been patchwork since the book burning.

sentences.zh: 古代之所更立者，遂有闕焉。

translations.literal: What antiquity had renewed thereafter stood incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient recovery remained flawed.

sentences.zh: 曹氏繫世，出自有虞氏，今祀圜丘，以始祖帝舜配，號圜丘曰皇皇帝天；

translations.literal: The Cao lineage descends from Youyu clan—now sacrificing at the round altar they match Founder Emperor Shun; they title the round altar August August Emperor Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Wei claimed descent from Shun—Heaven's altar honored Shun as counterpart.

sentences.zh: 方丘所祭曰皇皇后地，以舜妃伊氏配；

translations.literal: what the square altar sacrifices is titled August August Empress Earth—matched with Shun's consort Lady Yi;
translations.idiomatic: Earth's altar paired Lady Yi.

sentences.zh: 天郊所祭曰皇天之神，以太祖武皇帝配；

translations.literal: what Heaven's suburban sacrifice honors is titled August Heaven Spirit—matched with Founder Emperor Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Southern suburb matched Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 地郊所祭曰皇地之祇，以武宣后配；

translations.literal: what Earth's suburban sacrifice honors is titled August Earth Spirit—matched with Empress Wuxuan;
translations.idiomatic: Northern suburb matched Lady Bian.

sentences.zh: 宗祀皇考高祖文皇帝於明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: In the Bright Hall they sacrifice to August Father Gaozu Emperor Wen as counterpart to High God.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall paired Cao Pi with High God.

sentences.zh: 」至晉泰始二年，并圜丘、方丘二至之祀於南北郊。〉

translations.literal: By Jin Taishi 2 they merged round-altar and square-altar solstice rites into north and south suburbs."
translations.idiomatic: Jin later fused the dual earth-heaven sites."

sentences.zh: 十二月壬子冬至，始祀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on day renzi at winter solstice, he first performed sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice renzi saw the first new ritual.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，分襄陽臨沮、宜城、旍陽、邔

translations.literal: On day dingsi he divided from Xiangyang the counties Linju, Yicheng, Jingyang, and Yi-
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi four Xiangyang counties—Linju, Yicheng, Jingyang, and Yi (graph splits across sentences)—were partitioned.

sentences.zh: 〈邔音其己反〉

translations.literal: Yi is read qi-ji fan (phonetic note).
translations.idiomatic: Phonetic gloss for the county name (fanqie: qi plus ji syllables).

sentences.zh: 四縣，置襄陽南部都尉。

translations.literal: four counties—establish southern Xiangyang commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Those four counties formed southern Xiangyang command.

sentences.zh: 己未，有司奏文昭皇后立廟京都。

translations.literal: On day jiwei the relevant offices memorialized to establish Empress Wenzhao's temple in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei officials asked a capital shrine for Lady Zhen.

sentences.zh: 分襄陽郡之鄀葉縣屬義陽郡。

translations.literal: He divided Ru and Ye counties from Xiangyang commandery to belong to Yiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ru and Ye moved from Xiangyang to Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：是歲，徙長安諸鐘簴、駱駝、銅人、承露盤。

translations.literal: The Wei Lue states: That year they moved Chang'an's bell racks, camels, bronze men, and dew basins.
translations.idiomatic: Wei looted Han bronze monuments from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 盤折，銅人重不可致，留于霸城。

translations.literal: The basin broke; the bronze men were too heavy to transport—left at Ba city.
translations.idiomatic: The dew dish snapped; giants stayed at Ba.

sentences.zh: 大發銅鑄作銅人二，號曰翁仲，列坐於司馬門外。

translations.literal: They greatly melted bronze to cast two bronze men, titled Wengzhong, seated in a row outside the Sima Gate.
translations.idiomatic: They recast bronze into two Wengzhong statues by Sima Gate.

sentences.zh: 又鑄黃龍、鳳皇各一，龍高四丈，鳳高三丈餘，置內殿前。

translations.literal: They also cast yellow dragon and phoenix, one each—dragon four zhang high, phoenix over three zhang—placed before the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: Monumental dragon and phoenix bronzes flanked the inner court.

sentences.zh: 起土山於芳林園西北陬，使公卿羣僚皆負土成山，樹松竹雜木善草於其上，捕山禽雜獸置其中。

translations.literal: They raised an earthen hill in Fanglin Garden's northwest corner, ordering dukes and ministers all to shoulder earth to complete the hill, planting pine, bamboo, mixed trees and fine grass atop it, capturing mountain birds and beasts to place within.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers packed earth for an imperial hunting mound in Fanglin.

sentences.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：帝徙盤，盤折，聲聞數十里，金狄或泣，因留於霸城。

translations.literal: The Han Jin Chunqiu states: When the Emperor moved the basin it broke—sound carried tens of li—bronze men reportedly wept—therefore they remained at Ba city.
translations.idiomatic: Legend says the Han bells shattered en route and wept bronze tears.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》載司徒軍議掾河東董尋上書諫曰：「臣聞古之直士，盡言於國，不避死亡。

translations.literal: The Wei Lue records Staff Counselor of the Minister of Education Dong Xun of Hedong memorializing: "Your servant has heard ancient straight officers exhausted speech for the state and did not avoid death.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xun cited fearless ancient remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 故周昌比高祖於桀、紂，劉輔譬趙后於人婢。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhou Chang compared Emperor Gao to Jie and Zhou; Liu Fu likened Empress Zhao to a slave girl.
translations.idiomatic: He named Zhou Chang and Liu Fu's blunt analogies.

sentences.zh: 天生忠直，雖白刃沸湯，往而不顧者，誠爲時主愛惜天下也。

translations.literal: Heaven breeds loyalty and straightness—though white blades and boiling soup—going forward without looking back—truly because they cherish all under heaven for the ruler of the age.
translations.idiomatic: True advisers brave death for the realm's sake.

sentences.zh: 建安以來，野戰死亡，或門殫戶盡，雖有存者，遺孤老弱。

translations.literal: Since Jian'an, field battles have killed—sometimes whole gates wiped out—though some survive, orphans and aged weak remain.
translations.idiomatic: Decades of war had beggared families.

sentences.zh: 若今宮室狹小，當廣大之，猶宜隨時，不妨農務，況乃作無益之物，黃龍、鳳皇，九龍、承露盤，土山、淵池，此皆聖明之所不興也，其功參倍於殿舍。

translations.literal: If now palace chambers are cramped and ought to be enlarged—still it should suit the season and not harm farming—how much more these useless things—yellow dragon, phoenix, Jiulong, dew basins, earthen hills, deep pools—these are what sage clarity does not raise—their labor costs several times palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Monuments wasted labor far beyond useful building.

sentences.zh: 三公九卿侍中尚書，天下至德，皆知非道而不敢言者，以陛下春秋方剛，心畏雷霆。

translations.literal: The three dukes, nine ministers, palace attendants, and ministers of the masters—the realm's highest virtue—all know it is wrong yet dare not speak—because Your Majesty's spring and autumn are still vigorous—they fear thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers stayed mute fearing a young emperor's wrath.

sentences.zh: 今陛下旣尊羣臣，顯以冠冕，被以文繡，載以華輿，所以異於小人；

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty already honors the host of ministers—displaying them with caps and sashes—covering them with patterned embroidery—carrying them in splendid carriages—thereby distinguishing them from petty men;
translations.idiomatic: High ministers rode in splendor—why humiliate them?

sentences.zh: 而使穿方舉土，面目垢黑，沾體塗足，衣冠了鳥，毀國之光以崇無益，甚非謂也。

translations.literal: yet You make them dig foundation pits and shoulder earth—faces black with grime—bodies smeared and feet mud-stained—caps and robes in tatters—destroying the state's glory to exalt the useless—this is far from appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Making nobles haul dirt ruined dignity for toys.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『君使臣以禮，臣事君以忠。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'The ruler employs ministers by ritual; ministers serve the ruler by loyalty.'
translations.idiomatic: He quoted Analects on mutual ritual.

sentences.zh: 』無忠無禮，國何以立！

translations.literal: Without loyalty or ritual—how does the state stand!
translations.idiomatic: Without mutual duty the state fails.

sentences.zh: 故有君不君，臣不臣，上下不通，心懷鬱結，使陰陽不和，災害屢降，凶惡之徒因閒而起，誰當爲陛下盡言是者乎？

translations.literal: Therefore there is ruler not ruler, minister not minister, above and below not communicating—hearts knotted in gloom—making yin and yang not harmonious—disasters repeatedly descend—villains seize gaps to rise—who will exhaust speech to Your Majesty on this?
translations.idiomatic: Silence breeds cosmic disorder and traitors.

sentences.zh: 又誰當干萬乘以死爲戲乎？

translations.literal: Further who will brave the ten-thousand-chariot ruler with death as sport?
translations.idiomatic: Who else would speak truth to power?

sentences.zh: 臣知言出必死，而臣自比於牛之一毛，生旣無益，死亦何損？

translations.literal: Your servant knows speech must mean death—yet your servant compares himself to one hair on an ox—alive without benefit—what harm in death?
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xun called his life negligible.

sentences.zh: 秉筆流涕，心與世辭。

translations.literal: Grasping brush with streaming tears—heart bidding farewell to the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote through tears, ready to die.

sentences.zh: 臣有八子，臣死之後，累陛下矣！

translations.literal: Your servant has eight sons—after your servant's death they will burden Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: He begged mercy for his eight sons.

sentences.zh: 」將奏，沐浴。

translations.literal: When about to memorialize he bathed.
translations.idiomatic: He purified himself before submitting.

sentences.zh: 旣通，帝曰：「董尋不畏死邪！

translations.literal: When it had passed through the Emperor said, "Does Dong Xun not fear death!
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi asked if Dong Xun feared execution.

sentences.zh: 」主者奏收尋，有詔勿問。

translations.literal: The chief officials memorialized to seize Xun—an edict said do not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Censors wanted him arrested—the emperor spared him.

sentences.zh: 後爲貝丘令，清省得民心。〉

translations.literal: Later he became magistrate of Beiqiu—clean and frugal—winning the people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xun later ruled Beiqiu honestly."

sentences.zh: 二年春正月，詔太尉司馬宣王帥衆討遼東。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, he ordered Grand Commandant Sima Yi to command the host and punish Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu 2 opened with Sima Yi's Liaodong expedition.

sentences.zh: 〈干竇《晉紀》曰：帝問宣王：「度淵將何計以待君？

translations.literal: Gan Bao's Jin Ji states: The Emperor asked Sima Yi, "How do you estimate Yuan will plan to await you?
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao records Mingdi quizzing Sima Yi on Gongsun Yuan.

sentences.zh: 」宣王對曰：「淵棄城預走，上計也；

translations.literal: Sima Yi replied: "If Yuan abandons the city and flees beforehand—that is the best plan;
translations.idiomatic: Best case: Yuan runs.

sentences.zh: 據遼水拒大軍，其次也；

translations.literal: holding the Liao River to refuse the great army—that is second;
translations.idiomatic: Second: defend the Liao River."

sentences.zh: 坐守襄平，此爲成禽耳。

translations.literal: Sitting and defending Xiangping—this is to become captured game.
translations.idiomatic: If he only sits in Xiangping, we will bag him like game.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「然則三者何出？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Then of the three outcomes which will occur?"
translations.idiomatic: "Which of the three stratagems will he choose?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「唯明智審量彼我，乃預有所割棄，此旣非淵所及，又謂今往縣遠，不能持久，必先拒遼水，後守也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Only clear wisdom that examines enemy and self can foresee what to abandon beforehand—this is beyond Yuan's reach; further they consider the march distant and unable to endure long—he must first refuse the army at the Liao River, afterward defend the city."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi expected Yuan to lack foresight—long supply lines would force him to hold the Liao first, then the walls.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「往還幾日？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "How many days round trip?"
translations.idiomatic: "How long is the full campaign?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「往百日，攻百日；

translations.literal: He replied: "Go one hundred days, attack one hundred days;
translations.idiomatic: "One hundred days out, one hundred besieging."

sentences.zh: 還百日，以六十日爲休息，如此，一年足矣。

translations.literal: return one hundred days—using sixty days for rest—thus one year suffices."
translations.idiomatic: One hundred back plus sixty rest—twelve months all told."

sentences.zh: 」魏名臣奏載散騎常侍何曾表曰：「臣聞先王制法，必於全慎，故建官授任，則置假輔，陳師命將，則立監貳，宣命遣使，則設介副，臨敵交刃，則參御右，蓋以盡謀思之功，防安危之變也。

translations.literal: Wei Mingchen Zou records Palace Attendant He Zeng's memorial: "Your servant has heard former kings in establishing law must be wholly cautious—therefore when establishing offices and granting appointment they set deputy assistants; when deploying hosts and appointing generals they establish overseers and seconds; when proclaiming orders and dispatching envoys they set deputies; when facing the enemy and crossing blades they assign chariot companions on the right—by these means they exhaust planning thought and guard against safety-peril shifts.
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng cited ancient practice of seconds on campaign—deputy commanders for contingency.

sentences.zh: 是以在險當難，則權足相濟，隕缺不預，則手足相代，其爲固防，至深至遠。

translations.literal: Therefore in peril and facing hardship authority suffices to aid each other; if disability strikes unexpectedly then hands and feet replace one another—such solid defense reaches deepest and farthest.
translations.idiomatic: Seconds cover emergencies—true defense runs deep.

sentences.zh: 及至漢氏，亦循舊章。

translations.literal: Coming down to Han times they also followed the old pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Han followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 韓信伐趙，張耳爲貳；

translations.literal: When Han Xin attacked Zhao, Zhang Er was second;
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin had Zhang Er as deputy against Zhao.

sentences.zh: 馬援討越，劉隆副軍。

translations.literal: When Ma Yuan punished the Yue, Liu Long was assistant army.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan took Liu Long on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 前世之迹，著在篇志。

translations.literal: Former generations' traces are plain in documents.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent fills the histories.

sentences.zh: 今懿奉辭誅罪，步騎數萬，道路迴阻，四千餘里，雖假天威，有征無戰，寇或潛遁，消散日月，命無常期。

translations.literal: Now Yi receives orders to punish crime—infantry and cavalry several tens of thousands—roads winding and blocked—over four thousand li—although borrowing Heaven's might there is campaign without battle—yet the bandit may slip away and vanish in days and months—fate has no fixed term.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong was four thousand li—Yuan might flee and drag out time.

sentences.zh: 人非金石，遠慮詳備，誠宜有副。

translations.literal: Men are not metal and stone—far planning detailed and complete—truly ought to have a deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Mortals need a second-in-command for a distant war.

sentences.zh: 今北邊諸將及懿所督，皆爲僚屬，名位不殊，素無定分，卒有變急，不相鎮攝。

translations.literal: Now northern frontier generals and those supervised by Yi are all staff subordinates—names and ranks not distinguished—ordinarily no fixed hierarchy—if sudden crisis comes they will not restrain each other.
translations.idiomatic: Northern officers lacked clear chain under Sima Yi—crisis could bring chaos.

sentences.zh: 存不忘亡，聖達所戒，宜選大臣名將威重宿著者，盛其禮秩，遣詣懿軍，進同謀略，退爲副佐。

translations.literal: Remembering survival forget not death—what sages teach—ought to select great ministers and famed generals of awesome weight long renowned—enrich their ritual rank—dispatch them to Yi's army—advancing share counsel—retreating serve as deputy assistants.
translations.idiomatic: He urged sending a senior deputy to Sima Yi's camp.

sentences.zh: 雖有萬一不虞之災，軍主有儲，則無患矣。

translations.literal: Although there may be one-in-ten-thousand unforeseen disaster—if the army chief has reserve—then there is no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: A backup commander contained risk.

sentences.zh: 」毌丘儉志記云，時以儉爲宣王副也。〉

translations.literal: Guanqiu Jian's memoir states at that time they appointed Jian as Sima Yi's deputy."
translations.idiomatic: The note identifies Guanqiu Jian as that deputy."

sentences.zh: 秋八月，燒當羌王芒中、注詣等叛，涼州刺史率諸郡攻討，斬注詣首。

translations.literal: In autumn, eighth month, Shaodang Qiang king Mangzhong, Zhuyi, and others rebelled; the Inspector of Liangzhou led commanderies to attack and punish them—beheaded Zhuyi's head.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn: Shaodang Qiang rose; Liangzhou forces killed Zhuyi.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，有彗星見張宿。

translations.literal: On day guichou a comet appeared in Zhang constellation.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou a comet streaked through Zhang.

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：史官言於帝曰：「此周之分野也，洛邑惡之。

translations.literal: The Han Jin Chunqiu states: The historian reported to the Emperor: "This is Zhou's field division—Luoyi dreads it.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomers tied the comet to Zhou's asterism—ill for Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 」於是大脩禳禱之術以厭焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon they greatly practiced exorcism and prayer techniques to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: The court staged grand apotropaic rites.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：九月，蜀陰平太守廖惇反，攻守善羌侯宕蕈營。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu states: In the ninth month Shu Yinping grand warden Liao Dun rebelled, attacking and besieging Shanchan Qiang chief Dangxun's camp.
translations.idiomatic: September: Shu's Yinping governor mutinied against the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史郭淮遣廣魏太守王贇、南安太守游弈將兵討惇。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yongzhou Guo Huai dispatched Guangwei grand warden Wang Yun and Nan'an grand warden You Yi leading troops to punish Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai sent Wang Yun and You Yi against Liao Dun.

sentences.zh: 淮上書：「贇、弈等分兵夾山東西，圍落賊表，破在旦夕。

translations.literal: Huai memorialized: "Yun and Yi divided troops east and west of the mountain, surrounding the bandits' outer ring—victory within dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai reported a tight pincer—victory imminent.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「兵勢惡離。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Military momentum hates splitting."
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi warned against divided forces.

sentences.zh: 」促詔淮勑弈諸別營非要處者，還令據便地。

translations.literal: He urgently ordered Huai to instruct Yi's detached camps not at vital points to return and seize convenient ground.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered consolidation before the edict arrived.

sentences.zh: 詔勑未到，弈軍爲惇所破；

translations.literal: Before the edict arrived Yi's army was broken by Dun;
translations.idiomatic: Too late—You Yi was routed.

sentences.zh: 贇爲流矢所中死。〉

translations.literal: Yun was struck by a stray arrow and died."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun fell to a stray shaft."

sentences.zh: 丙寅，司馬宣王圍公孫淵於襄平，大破之，傳淵首于京都，海東諸郡平。

translations.literal: On day bingyin Sima Yi besieged Gongsun Yuan at Xiangping—greatly defeated him—sent Yuan's head to the capital—the eastern sea commanderies were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Sima Yi took Xiangping and shipped Yuan's head south.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，錄討淵功，太尉宣王以下增邑封爵各有差。

translations.literal: In winter, eleventh month, they recorded merit in punishing Yuan—below Grand Commandant Sima Yi—added fief and noble rank by grade.
translations.idiomatic: Winter rewards went to Sima Yi and subordinates.

sentences.zh: 初，帝議遣宣王討淵，發卒四萬人。

translations.literal: At first when the Emperor debated dispatching Sima Yi to punish Yuan he mobilized forty thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong expedition began with forty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 議臣皆以爲四萬兵多，役費難供。

translations.literal: Counselors all thought forty thousand troops too many—labor costs hard to supply.
translations.idiomatic: Critics called forty thousand excessive.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「四千里征伐，雖云用奇，亦當任力，不當稍計役費。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "A four-thousand-li expedition—even if called using strangeness—still must rely on strength—ought not slightly reckon labor expense."
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi insisted distance demanded numbers—cost was secondary.

sentences.zh: 」遂以四萬人行。

translations.literal: Thereupon forty thousand men marched.
translations.idiomatic: Forty thousand went east.

sentences.zh: 及宣王至遼東，霖雨不得時攻，羣臣或以爲淵未可卒破，宜詔宣王還。
