translations.literal: When Sima Yi reached Liaodong ceaseless rains prevented timely attack—some ministers thought Yuan could not be quickly broken—ought to order Sima Yi back.
translations.idiomatic: Rain stalled the siege; courtiers wanted recall.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「司馬懿臨危制變，擒淵可計日待也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Sima Yi masters emergencies and controls changes—capturing Yuan can be awaited counted days.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi trusted Sima Yi to finish within days.

sentences.zh: 」卒皆如所策。

translations.literal: In the end all matched what he calculated.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as predicted.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以司空衞臻爲司徒，司隷校尉崔林爲司空。

translations.literal: On day renwu he appointed Minister of Works Wei Zhen Minister of Education and Metropolitan Commandant Cui Lin Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Wei Zhen headed education and Cui Lin works.

sentences.zh: 閏月，月犯心中央大星。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month the moon trespassed the great central star of Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary month: lunar occultation of Antares.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙丑，帝寢疾不豫。

translations.literal: On day yichou in the twelfth month the Emperor lay gravely ill and unwell.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth-month yichou Mingdi took to bed.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，立皇后。

translations.literal: On day xinsi he established an empress.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi he named an empress.

sentences.zh: 賜天下男子爵人二級，鰥寡孤獨穀。

translations.literal: He bestowed on the men of the realm two ranks each; grain to widowers, widows, orphans, and solitary.
translations.idiomatic: General ranks and grain like earlier reigns.

sentences.zh: 以燕王宇爲大將軍，甲申免，以武衞將軍曹爽代之。

translations.literal: He appointed Prince of Yan Yu Grand General—on day jiashen dismissed him—General Who Guards the Martial Cao Shuang replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yu briefly held grand general—then Cao Shuang replaced him on jiashen.

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：帝以燕王宇爲大將軍，使與領軍將軍夏侯獻、武衞將軍曹爽、屯騎校尉曹肈、驍騎將軍秦朗等對輔政。

translations.literal: The Han Jin Chunqiu states: The Emperor appointed Prince of Yan Yu Grand General—ordering him with General Who Commands the Army Xiahou Xian, General Who Guards the Martial Cao Shuang, Colonel of Garrisoned Cavalry Cao Zhao, General of Valiant Cavalry Qin Lang and others to balance regency.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yu was to share power with Xiahou Xian, Shuang, Zhao, and Lang.

sentences.zh: 中書監劉放、令孫資久專權寵，爲朗等素所不善，懼有後害，陰圖間之，而宇常在帝側，故未得有言。

translations.literal: Palace Writers Supervisor Liu Fang and Director Sun Zi long monopolized favor and power—Lang and others had never liked them—they feared later harm—secretly plotted to estrange them—but Yu constantly stood at the Emperor's side—therefore they had no chance to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang and Sun Zi feared Cao Yu's regency while he blocked access.

sentences.zh: 甲申，帝氣微，宇下殿呼曹肈有所議，未還，而帝少間，惟曹爽獨在。

translations.literal: On day jiashen the Emperor's breath grew faint—Yu descended the hall summoning Cao Zhao to consult—before he returned the Emperor improved slightly—only Cao Shuang remained alone.
translations.idiomatic: A bedside shuffle left only Cao Shuang when Yu stepped out.

sentences.zh: 放知之，呼資與謀。

translations.literal: Fang knew it—summoned Zi to plot.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang alerted Sun Zi.

sentences.zh: 資曰：「不可動也。

translations.literal: Zi said: "We cannot move."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zi hesitated.

sentences.zh: 」放曰：「俱入鼎鑊，何不可之有？

translations.literal: Fang said: "Both enter the cauldron—what cannot be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang said they faced execution either way.

sentences.zh: 」乃突前見帝，垂泣曰：「陛下氣微，若有不諱，將以天下付誰？

translations.literal: They suddenly advanced to see the Emperor—weeping said: "Your Majesty's breath is faint—if there is misfortune—to whom will You entrust all under heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: They forced a deathbed choice of regents.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿不聞用燕王耶？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Have you not heard—employ Prince of Yan?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant Cao Yu.

sentences.zh: 」放曰：「陛下忘先帝詔勑，藩王不得輔政。

translations.literal: Fang said: "Your Majesty forgets the late Emperor's edict—feudal kings must not assist government.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang cited the ban on princely regency.

sentences.zh: 且陛下方病，而曹肈、秦朗等便與才人侍疾者言戲。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty is just ill—yet Cao Zhao and Qin Lang jest with the talented ladies attending illness.
translations.idiomatic: He smeared Zhao and Lang for flirting with nurses.

sentences.zh: 燕王擁兵南面，不聽臣等入，此即豎刀、趙高也。

translations.literal: Prince of Yan embraces troops facing south—will not hear us ministers enter—this is Shudiao and Zhao Gao.
translations.idiomatic: He compared Cao Yu to classic usurping eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 今皇太子幼弱，未能統政，外有彊暴之寇，內有勞怨之民，陛下不遠慮存亡，而近係恩舊。

translations.literal: Now the heir apparent is young and weak—unable to govern—without lies fierce bandits—within laboring resentful people—Your Majesty does not plan far for survival and extinction—yet bind Yourself to old kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He warned of weak heir and foreign foes.

sentences.zh: 委祖考之業，付二三凡士，寢疾數日，外內擁隔，社稷危殆，而己不知，此臣等所以痛心也。

translations.literal: Entrusting ancestral and examining fathers' enterprise to two or three mediocre men—lying ill several days—inner and outer blocked apart—altar and grain imperiled—yet You do not know—this is why your servants' hearts ache.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre regents would doom the state.

sentences.zh: 」帝得放言，大怒曰：「誰可任者？

translations.literal: Hearing Fang's words the Emperor grew greatly angry and said: "Who can be appointed?"
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi angrily asked alternatives.

sentences.zh: 」放、資乃舉爽代宇，又白「宜詔司馬宣王使相參」，帝從之。

translations.literal: Fang and Zi thereupon raised Shuang to replace Yu—also stated "ought to order Sima Yi to join consultation"—the Emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: They installed Cao Shuang plus Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 放、資出，曹肈入，泣涕固諫，帝使肈勑停。

translations.literal: Fang and Zi exited—Cao Zhao entered—weeping firmly remonstrated—the Emperor ordered Zhao to command halt.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhao protested the coup—brief halt.

sentences.zh: 肈出戶，放、資趨而往，復說止帝，帝又從其言。

translations.literal: Zhao left the door—Fang and Zi hurried after—again persuaded stopping the Emperor—the Emperor again followed their words.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and Zi overruled Zhao twice.

sentences.zh: 放曰：「宜爲手詔。

translations.literal: Fang said: "Ought to make a handwritten edict."
translations.idiomatic: "We need your seal in your own hand."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我困篤，不能。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I am desperately tired—cannot."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could barely write.

sentences.zh: 」放即上牀，執帝手強作之，遂齎出，大言曰：「有詔免燕王宇等官，不得停省中。

translations.literal: Fang then mounted the bed—grasped the Emperor's hand—forced it to write—thereupon carried it out—shouting loudly: "There is an edict dismissing Prince of Yan Yu and others from office—may not linger in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang guided Mingdi's hand to dismiss Cao Yu.

sentences.zh: 」於是宇、肈、獻、朗相與泣而歸第。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon Yu, Zhao, Xian, and Lang together wept and returned to their mansions."
translations.idiomatic: The princely regents were sent home weeping."

sentences.zh: 初，青龍三年中，壽春農民妻自言爲天神所下，命爲登女，當營衞帝室，蠲邪納福。

translations.literal: At first in Qinglong 3 a Shouchun farmer's wife declared herself sent down by Heaven's spirit—ordered to be Deng woman—ought to camp guarding the imperial house—dispelling evil and bringing blessing.
translations.idiomatic: A Shouchun woman claimed divine possession—Qinglong 3.

sentences.zh: 飲人以水，及以洗創，或多愈者。

translations.literal: She gave people water to drink and to wash wounds—many were cured.
translations.idiomatic: Her water supposedly healed.

sentences.zh: 於是立館後宮，下詔稱揚，甚見優寵。

translations.literal: Thereupon they established a lodge in the rear palace—issued edict praising her—she received lavish favor.
translations.idiomatic: The court housed and praised her.

sentences.zh: 及帝疾，飲水無驗，於是殺焉。

translations.literal: When the Emperor fell ill drinking water showed no effect—thereupon they killed her.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingdi sickened her magic failed—she was executed.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月丁亥，太尉宣王還至河內，帝驛馬召到，引入卧內，執其手謂曰：「吾疾甚，以後事屬君，君其與爽輔少子。

translations.literal: In the third year, spring, first month, on day dinghai Grand Commandant Sima Yi returned to He interior—the Emperor by relay horse summoned him—led him into the bedchamber—grasped his hand saying: "My illness is severe—I entrust later affairs to you—you shall assist the young son together with Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Dinghai: Sima Yi reached Hongnong—Mingdi gripped his hand for the deathbed pact.

sentences.zh: 吾得見君，無所恨！

translations.literal: Having seen you I have no regret!
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Sima Yi fulfilled his last wish.

sentences.zh: 」宣王頓首流涕。

translations.literal: Sima Yi knocked head and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi kowtowed in tears.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：帝旣從劉放計，召司馬宣王，自力爲詔，旣封，顧呼宮中常所給使者曰：「辟邪來！

translations.literal: The Wei Lue states: After the Emperor followed Liu Fang's plan summoning Sima Yi—he personally drafted the edict—when sealed—turned calling the usual palace messenger: "Bixie come!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lue describes the sealed summons to Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 汝持我此詔授太尉也。

translations.literal: You take this edict of mine and deliver it to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Hand this edict to the grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 」辟邪馳去。

translations.literal: Bixie galloped off.
translations.idiomatic: The runner Bixie dashed away.

sentences.zh: 先是，燕王爲帝畫計，以爲關中事重，宜便道遣宣王從河內西還，事以施行。

translations.literal: Earlier Prince of Yan had planned for the Emperor—considering Guanzhong affairs weighty—ought by convenient route order Sima Yi return west from He interior—the matter was already implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yu had already routed Sima Yi toward Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 宣王得前詔，斯須復得後手筆，疑京師有變，乃馳到，入見帝。

translations.literal: Sima Yi received the prior edict—momentarily again received later handwritten note—suspected change in the capital—thereupon galloped to arrive—entered and saw the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Conflicting orders brought Sima Yi racing to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 勞問訖，乃召齊、秦二王以示宣王，別指齊王謂宣王曰：「此是也，君諦視之，勿誤也！

translations.literal: After consoling finished he summoned Qi and Qin two princes to show Sima Yi—separately pointing at Qi prince telling Sima Yi: "This is the one—look carefully—do not mistake!
translations.idiomatic: He pointed out Prince Fang as heir.

sentences.zh: 」又教齊王令前抱宣王頸。

translations.literal: He also instructed Qi prince to come forward and hug Sima Yi's neck.
translations.idiomatic: Young Fang embraced Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：時太子芳年八歲，秦王九歲，在于御側。

translations.literal: The Wei Shi Chunqiu states: At that time Crown Prince Fang was eight sui—Qin prince nine—standing at the imperial side.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was eight, the Qin prince nine.

sentences.zh: 帝執宣王手，目太子曰：「死乃復可忍，朕忍死待君，君其與爽輔此。

translations.literal: The Emperor grasped Sima Yi's hand—eyeing the crown prince said: "Death then again can be endured—I endure death awaiting you—you shall assist this together with Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi made Fang's succession explicit.

sentences.zh: 」宣王曰：「陛下不見先帝屬臣以陛下乎？」〉

translations.literal: Sima Yi said: "Does Your Majesty not see how the late Emperor entrusted Your Majesty to your servant?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi invoked Cao Pi's trust."

sentences.zh: 即日，帝崩于嘉福殿，

translations.literal: That same day the Emperor died in Jiafu Hall,
translations.idiomatic: He died that day in Jiafu Hall.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：殯于九龍前殿。〉

translations.literal: The Wei Shu states: Lying in repose before Jiulong Hall."
translations.idiomatic: The lying-in-state was before Jiulong Hall."

sentences.zh: 時年三十六。

translations.literal: At the time age thirty-six sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-six by civil reckoning.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之桉：魏武以建安九年八月定鄴，文帝始納甄后，明帝應以十年生，計至此年正月，整三十四年耳。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi submits: Emperor Wu took Ye in Jian'an 9 eighth month—Emperor Wen first took Empress Zhen—Emperor Ming ought to have been born tenth year—reckoning to this year's first month—full thirty-four years only.
translations.idiomatic: Pei argues Mingdi died at thirty-four not thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 時改正朔，以故年十二月爲今年正月，可彊名三十五年，不得三十六也。〉

translations.literal: At that time they changed the calendar—therefore old year's twelfth month became this year's first month—one could forcibly call thirty-five—cannot be thirty-six."
translations.idiomatic: Calendar reform inflated his recorded age."

sentences.zh: 癸丑，葬高平陵。

translations.literal: On day guichou he was buried at Gaoping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou he went to Gaoling tomb.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：帝容止可觀，望之儼然。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu states: The Emperor's bearing and deportment were worth viewing—gazing at him majestic.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu praises his majestic presence.

sentences.zh: 自在東宮，不交朝臣，不問政事，唯潛思書籍而已。

translations.literal: While in the Eastern Palace he did not associate with court ministers—did not inquire into governance affairs—only secretly pondered books.
translations.idiomatic: As heir he studied books and avoided faction.

sentences.zh: 即位之後，褒禮大臣，料簡功能，真偽不得相貿，務絕浮華譖毀之端，行師動衆，論決大事，謀臣將相咸服帝之大略。

translations.literal: After mounting the throne he honored ritual toward great ministers—evaluated merit and function—true and false could not trade places—strove to cut off flashy slander roots—when marching hosts and moving masses—deciding great affairs—counseling ministers and commanding generals alike submitted to the Emperor's grand strategy.
translations.idiomatic: His reign mixed meritocracy and decisive war policy.

sentences.zh: 性特彊識，雖左右小臣官簿性行，名跡所履，及其父兄子弟，一經耳目，終不遺忘。

translations.literal: His nature especially strong in memory—although petty ministers at left and right—their office registers nature and conduct—tracks trodden—and their fathers elder brothers sons younger brothers—once seen or heard—never forgot.
translations.idiomatic: He memorized every clerk's dossier.

sentences.zh: 含垢藏疾，容受直言，聽受吏民士庶上書，一月之中至數十百封，雖文辭鄙陋，猶覽省究竟，意無猒倦。

translations.literal: He endured stain and hid illness—accepted straight speech—heard and received clerks commoners gentlemen and common memorials—within one month reaching several tens to hundred seals—although literary phrasing was vulgar—still examined to the end—mind never weary.
translations.idiomatic: He read mountains of plebeian petitions.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：聞之長老，魏明帝天姿秀出，立髮垂地，口吃少言，而沉毅好斷。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: Hearing from elders—Wei Emperor Ming heaven's bearing outstanding—hair hanging to ground when standing—stammer few words—yet deep firm fond of deciding.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng describes his appearance and stutter.

sentences.zh: 初，諸公受遺輔導，帝皆以方任處之，政自己出。

translations.literal: At first the dukes receiving testament to assist instruction—the Emperor all placed them in regional posts—government issued from himself.
translations.idiomatic: He sidelined regents to frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 而優禮大臣，開容善直，雖犯顏極諫，無所摧戮，其君人之量如此之偉也。

translations.literal: Yet honoring ritual toward great ministers—open countenance toward good straight speech—although offending face extreme remonstrance—none were struck down—his capacity as ruler was thus vast.
translations.idiomatic: He tolerated blunt advisers.

sentences.zh: 然不思建德垂風，不固維城之基，至使大權偏據，社稷無衞，悲夫！〉

translations.literal: Yet he did not think to establish virtue and hang down wind—did not strengthen walls of the realm—until great power leaned aside—altar and grain without guard—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng laments weak princes and lost power to Sima."

sentences.zh: 評曰：明帝沉毅斷識，任心而行，蓋有君人之至槩焉。

translations.literal: Appraisal says: Emperor Ming was deep firm decisive in judgment—acting following mind—indeed had utmost bearing of a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou praises his ruler's spine.

sentences.zh: 于時百姓彫弊，四海分崩，不先聿脩顯祖，闡拓洪基，而遽追秦皇、漢武，宮館是營，格之遠猷，其殆疾乎！

translations.literal: At that time hundred surnames were carved and exhausted—four seas split and collapsed—he did not first cultivate illustrious ancestors—expand vast foundation—yet hastily pursued First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han—palaces and lodges were his enterprise—measured against far-reaching plans—perhaps sick indeed!
